## Source: sdk/AGENTS.md

# Build an Ether plugin

## The mental model (read this first)

A plugin is a manifest plus a request handler. **Kind** decides where the owner
finds it; **capabilities** advertise behavior; **contributes** describes that
behavior; **permissions** request access. A capability never grants permission.
Hosted TypeScript/JavaScript runs in QuickJS inside wazero, not Node: no process,
filesystem, npm resolution, or direct network. Export `handle(req)` returning
`{status, headers?, body}`. Use the synchronous permission-checked `ether` global.
Bundle SDK imports before packaging. Go/Python can run as HTTP/tunnel sidecars;
remote plugins have their own OS permissions and cannot use hosted folders or
SecretGet. Read current settings per request; persist state in KV, not globals.
Start with one useful result. Do work only on a viewer/owner request or an
explicitly configured job; page results and bound work so playback comes first.

The schema and generated reference are authoritative. Do not invent APIs from
method names. Open `/ether/plugins/reference/getting-started` in your server,
then search for the exact symbol. [Reference maintenance](../docs/plugin-developer-reference.md).

## Files

```text
my-plugin/
  manifest.json               # identity, runtime, permissions, contributions
  src/index.ts                # hosted handler (or plugin.py for a sidecar)
  dist/plugin.js              # compiled hosted artifact, generated by pack/load
  settings.schema.json        # referenced by ether.settings.$ref
  i18n/en.json                # English fallback for every $t:key
  assets/icon.svg             # optional icon
  tests/fixtures.json         # recorded request/expected-response cases
  README.md                   # setup and permission explanation
```

Paths in the manifest are package-relative and must stay inside the package.
Never ship credentials, node_modules, private media, or absolute local paths.

## First run: exact commands

From an Ether checkout, build the CLI once (pure Go):

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o ./ether ./cmd/ether
./ether plugin new catalogue --lang ts ./my-plugin
./ether plugin check ./my-plugin
./ether plugin test ./my-plugin
./ether plugin pack -o ./my-plugin.etherpkg ./my-plugin
```

With a **local development server you control** already running, set ETHER_TOKEN
to its admin token in your shell and run:

```sh
./ether plugin dev ./my-plugin --server http://localhost:32400
# Save src/index.ts: compile, install, and read logs. Ctrl-C stops watching.
# One install without a watcher:
./ether plugin dev ./my-plugin --server http://localhost:32400 --once
```

Alternatively open Plugins → Add and upload `my-plugin.etherpkg`. Review
requested permissions and enable it. Do not use a production server for iteration.
`check --json` is the structured report for agents. `dev` installs hosted
packages; remote Python/Go sidecars must run separately and be connected by
manifest URL or tunnel. `test` also runs recorded
fixtures; ETHER_BIN enables its headless integration check, ETHER_PLUGIN_URL tests
an already running remote sidecar. `pack` compiles TypeScript and checks the
package. No separate npm install is needed for generated hosted templates.

Ether reads the official signed marketplace (`https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`,
served at `https://braedonsaunders.github.io/ether-plugins/index.json`) by default
under Plugins → Marketplace. To publish a plugin there, upload `<id>-<version>.etherpkg`
to a GitHub release, run `./ether plugin publish --url <release-asset-url> ./my-plugin`
to pack the archive and print a validated `plugins/<id>.yaml` entry with its SHA-256
digest, and open a pull request against `https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`.
Marketplace CI verifies the artifact digest and runs `ether plugin check` before
signing the updated index.

## Manifest decisions

| Field | What to set |
|---|---|
| id, version, name | Stable lower-case reverse DNS ID, SemVer, readable name (≤60 characters) |
| description | Sentence case, ≤300 characters |
| types, resources, catalogs, idPrefixes | Stremio types, routes, catalog IDs and identifier prefixes actually served |
| ether.protocol | `1` |
| ether.kind | `source`, `integration`, `notification_channel`, `livetv_source`, `extension`, or `content` |
| ether.capabilities | Only implemented capabilities; the validator checks allowed kinds |
| ether.summary | ≤80 characters, or `$t:summary` with English fallback |
| ether.runtime | Hosted: `{kind:"hosted",entry:"src/index.ts"}` (or WASM `module`); remote: `{kind:"remote"}` |
| ether.permissions | Network hostnames (not URLs), catalog `read`, collections `write`, folders `read`, named secrets, viewers, sources `search`/`acquire`; omit access you do not need |
| ether.settings | Inline `{fields:[...]}` or `{"$ref":"settings.schema.json"}` |
| ether.strings | Locale → package file or inline object; `en` required for `$t:` labels |
| ether.contributes | Capability descriptors (`listSources`, `posterBadges`, `rankingSteps`, `ruleConditions`, etc.), pages, slots, commands, setup steps, mediaKinds (including `library.card` `poster\|landscape\|square`, `library.dateDisplay` `year\|date`, up to 50 `library.tabs` of `recommended\|library\|collections\|people\|view\|live` with optional `facet`/`order`/`search`/`searchPlaceholder`/`sort`/`direction` on `collections` tabs, required people-type `facet` plus optional `order` `name\|count`, `search`, and `searchPlaceholder` on `people` tabs, optional `layout` `grid\|list\|timeline`, `sort` (including `lastViewed`), `direction`, `search`/`searchPlaceholder`, and `filters` on `view` tabs supporting declared indexed fields and per-viewer state rules, optional `card` `landscape\|poster\|square` plus `search`/`searchPlaceholder` on `live` tabs backed by `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/live` and `/live/resolve`, and optional `browse.expand` `{facets, ttlHours?}` for background slice expansion); see generated types |
| ether.schedule | `[{every:"1h",call:"/ether/refresh"}]`; intervals ≥15 minutes, bounded idempotent work |
| ether.cluster | `leader` (default), or `every_node` only when each node must run it |
| ether.health | Optional interval ≥15 seconds |
| ether.author, license, repo, icon | Attribution, SPDX license, repository URL, SVG path |
| ether.sidecar | Remote launch instructions: docker, download, command, docs |
| ether.stremio | `true` for a native plugin that retains Stremio add-on routes |

Copy rules apply to contribution labels too: sentence case, no exclamation marks,
no em/en dashes, no “simply”, “just”, or “easily”. Setting secrets are sealed by
Ether; read with SecretGet only where needed, never echo them into views/logs.

## Capability → routes → host services

| Capability | Plugin surface | Host services commonly needed |
|---|---|---|
| list_source | contributes.listSources + `/catalog/{type}/{id}.json` | HTTPFetch, CatalogSearch/Get, KV |
| poster_badges | contributes.posterBadges (up to 4 sets) | BadgesSet/Clear/Usage, HTTPFetch, KV |
| catalog_provider | mediaKinds; paged browse/changes/expand or push | KindUpsert/Delete/Items, KV |
| kind_resolver / matcher | kind resolve/match handlers | ResolveSources, CachePut/Open/Delete; sources permission |
| stream_source / debrid_provider | Stremio stream; lazy open / debrid routes | HTTPFetch, SecretGet |
| metadata | `/meta/{type}/{id}.json`, contributes.metadata | HTTPFetch, CatalogGet |
| notify / events | notify send/test; event subscribe (`POST /ether/event`) + custom `events.publish` | HTTPFetch, SecretGet, KV, PublishEvent (`ether.events.publish`) |
| flow_actions | `contributes.flowActions` + `POST /ether/v1/flow-actions/{key}` (with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key`) | KV (idempotency deduplication), HTTPFetch, PublishEvent |
| ui / tools | ViewSpec page/action or declared tool | Settings, KV; grant only data the action needs |
| livetv_channels | channels, guide, stream (kind livetv_source, or a content plugin that also has live channels) | HTTPFetch, KV |
| subtitles / markers | subtitle or marker routes and descriptors | HTTPFetch; download only after viewer picks |
| ranking_step / rule_condition | `rank_key` / `cond_match` | Log/abort only: deterministic, no I/O or clock |
| plugin_directory | declared add-on directories | HTTPFetch |
| frontend_adapter | authenticated protocol routes | StreamURL, KindVisible (<=500 IDs), KindBrowse for own items; viewer-authenticated adapter calls only; Ether serves bytes |
| onair_content / livetv_pack | declared feeds/segments/TV packs | Only services the handler actually needs |

Settings, KV, Log and NotifyOwner do not require an extra behavior capability.
ArchiveList/Open/Read/Extract handle plugin-cached ZIP, 7z (Copy/LZMA/LZMA2), and RAR 4/5.
Per-call byte reads (`cache.read`, `archive.open`, and summed `archive.read` lengths) scale with
the plugin's memory grant: `readBytes = clamp(memoryBytes/4, 8 MiB, 512 MiB)` (default 32 MiB → 8 MiB;
1 GiB → 256 MiB), exposed at runtime via `runtime.limits` (`ether.runtime.limits()` / `BlobHost.RuntimeLimits`).
Use `archive.open` when reading one member or stepping through one large file in ranges. Use
`archive.read(blob, reads)` (1..4096 `{member, offset, length}` items summing to `<= readBytes`) when
parsing many small or medium members from one archive in batches. Hosted QuickJS provides native UTF-8
`TextDecoder` and `TextEncoder` globals (`__ether_text_decode` / `__ether_text_encode`, or `decodeText` /
`encodeText` from `@ether/plugin-sdk`) so decoding `Uint8Array` slices into strings runs in native Go rather
than a per-byte JavaScript loop. Big media never goes through
`cache.read`, `archive.open`, or `archive.read` — Ether streams cached blobs and archive members
directly (`internal/plugins/frontend_blob.go`, `frontend.streamURL`); these calls are only for bytes
the plugin must parse. `ArchiveExtract(blob, memberIndex[, {libraryKey?, name?}])`
streams an uncompressed member into the plugin's library blob cache in one pass and returns
{ref, size, sha1, md5, crc32} without guest memory buffering. Solid ranges restart at the block beginning
per call; prefer large sequential chunks. Host memory/byte grants apply to
metadata, dictionaries and decoding. Split archives, encryption,
and special files are refused; `archive.list` flags unsafe member names as
informational warnings while by-index reads and extracts accept any
non-directory member. Other 7z coder chains are unsupported.

FoldersList/Stat/Hash need `folders:read` plus an owner-selected root; they return
metadata/digests, not bytes. Viewer access requires that viewer's grant.
Private LAN hosts stay blocked for HTTP fetch, fetchToCache, hash, and remote calls unless the owner allows the exact `host` or `host:port` under "On your network" in the plugin's settings (loopback stays blocked unless `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` is explicitly granted). Exact local hosts declared in `permissions.network` (dotless names, `.local`, `.lan`, `.home.arpa`, or private IPs) are shown on the install sheet and pre-granted when installed. For user-hosted services whose hostname comes from plugin settings, declare `"operator"` in `permissions.network` (never `"*"`); Ether prompts the owner to approve each server address per plugin before requests or stream resolvers admit it.
Host calls enforce permissions again on every request; revocation is immediate.

## Poster badges

A plugin with capability `poster_badges` declares up to 4 badge sets in
`ether.contributes.posterBadges: [{key, label, description?}]`, where `key`
matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`. Typical sets include a `"dub languages"` set
for an anime plugin (`{"key":"dub_languages","label":"Dub languages"}`) and an
`"editions"` set (`{"key":"editions","label":"Editions"}`).

Push or remove stored badge labels from an action, event, or scheduled run:

```ts
ether.badges.set("dub_languages", [
  { title: { type: "show", tmdb: 37854 }, labels: ["EN DUB", "JA"] },
]);
ether.badges.set("editions", [
  { title: { type: "movie", imdb: "tt0083658" }, labels: ["FINAL CUT"] },
]);
const usage = ether.badges.usage(); // { titles, quotaTitles }
// ether.badges.clear("editions");
```

`ether.badges.set(setKey, entries)` accepts up to 500 entries per call. Each
entry targets a `"movie"` or `"show"` by `tmdb` and/or `imdb` ID and supplies at
most 3 labels per title per set; an empty `labels` array deletes that title's
badges in the set. Each label is 1 to 16 characters from `[A-Z0-9 +&'./-]`;
lowercase input is uppercased, and any other character or length is rejected.
Each plugin may badge up to 200,000 titles (`ether.badges.usage()` reports
`{titles, quotaTitles}`). Ether draws the badges itself using the owner's poster
overlay style, the owner can switch each set off in Metadata -> Artwork
(`overlays.Settings.disabledBadgeSets` entries formatted as `"<pluginId>:<setKey>"`),
and no plugin call happens while rendering posters.

## Flows: custom events and actions

Plugins participate in Ether Flows in two additive ways (see `sdk/examples/smart-lights/`):

1. **Publish custom events** (`capabilities: ["events"]` + `ether.contributes.events.publish`):
   Declare typed event schemas (`key`, `version`, `label`, `fields`) alongside or instead of `events.subscribe` (which accepts both the 12 legacy EPP/1 names and canonical Flows event names). Published events are namespaced as `plugin:<pluginId>/<key>` on Ether's event bus and appear in the Flows trigger picker. Call `ether.events.publish(key, payload[, correlation])` in hosted plugins or `POST /ether/plugin-host/events/publish` from remote sidecars (`ctx.PublishEvent` in Go, `ctx.ether.events.publish` in TypeScript/Python). Payloads are schema-validated (max 64 KiB) and rate-limited to 30 events/minute per plugin (`rate_limited` / HTTP 429). Events emitted from inside a Flow action automatically inherit incremented `flowDepth` and `originRunId` for loop protection.
2. **Contribute Flow actions** (`capabilities: ["flow_actions"]` + `ether.contributes.flowActions`):
   Declare actions (`key`, `label`, `route` under `/ether/`, optional `timeout` up to `60s`, `idempotent`, `sideEffect`, `params`, `outputs`). Actions are registered atomically as `plugin:<pluginId>/<key>` on install, update, enable/disable, grant change, and uninstall. Ether invokes the route via `POST` with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` and JSON body `{flowId, runId, nodeId, idempotencyKey, dryRun, params}` and expects `{output: {...}, branch?}`. Always respect `dryRun` and deduplicate side effects using `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` in KV. In shadow mode, both `PublishEvent` and Flow action executions are journaled without external side effects.

## Per-route call limits and owner ceilings

Ether enforces the same deadline it advertises in `X-Ether-Deadline`. On viewer
paths, a hosted call's governance unit budget scales directly with that route's
deadline (`1 unit = 100 µs` of guest wall time, or `10,000 units/s`, plus priced
host calls; time spent inside a host call is bounded by the call deadline rather
than billed as guest wall time):

| Route group | Effective deadline | Effective unit budget |
|---|---|---|
| `/stream/*`, `/ether/open*` | 3 s (20 s for Stremio add-ons) | 30,000 units (200,000 for Stremio) |
| `/subtitles/*`, `/ether/subtitles/*` | 5 s (10 s for Stremio add-ons) | 50,000 units (100,000 for Stremio) |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/*/resolve`, `/ether/v1/kinds/*/match` | 5 s | 50,000 units |
| `/catalog/*`, `/meta/*`, `/ether/metadata/*`, `/ether/markers*`, `/ether/v1/kinds/*/search`, `/ether/v1/kinds/*/items/*` | 10 s (20 s for Stremio `/catalog/*`) | 100,000 units (200,000 for Stremio `/catalog/*`) |
| `/ether/options/*`, `/ether/view/*` | 2 s | Owner-granted ceiling |
| `/ether/configure`, `/ether/health` | 5 s | Owner-granted ceiling |
| `/ether/test` | 15 s | Owner-granted ceiling |
| Other protocol routes (`/ether/notify`, `/ether/v1/frontend/*`) | 30 s | Owner-granted ceiling |
| `/ether/v1/flow-actions/*` | Declared action `timeout` (default 30 s, max 60 s) | Owner-granted ceiling |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/*/browse`, `/ether/v1/kinds/*/changes`, `/ether/v1/kinds/*/expand`, `/ether/channels.json`, `/ether/guide/*`, `/ether/v1/setup/*`, `/ether/action/*`, `/ether/tool/*`, `/ether/event`, `/ether/job/*` | Owner-granted ceiling (default 12 h) | Owner-granted ceiling (default `2^60` units) |
| `rank_key`, `cond_match` | 2 ms per candidate, 50 ms per batch | Hot-path deterministic budget (log/abort only) |

Calling `ether.runtime.limits()` (`ctx.ether.runtime.limits()` in the TypeScript
SDK) inside a hosted handler returns the **effective** `deadline` and
`unitBudget` for the current call after route and owner clamps, alongside
`memoryBytes`, `readBytes`, `poolSize`, `fetchBytes`, `maxItems` and archive limits. If a viewer-path
call spends its whole budget, the error names the route and limit (for example
`used the whole 5 s budget for /ether/v1/kinds/games/resolve (50010/50000 units)`).

Plugins request higher memory, time, instance pool (`poolSize`, default 2, max 4),
download or archive limits in `ether.runtime.limits` in `manifest.json`. Background
jobs and sync calls hold at most `poolSize - 1` instances so viewer, adapter and
health calls retain a free instance; waiting for a busy instance returns a retryable
busy error instead of crashing the plugin or cancelling running jobs. Owners raise or lower the server-wide
ceilings in **Plugins → Settings**, or override them for a single plugin in that
plugin's drawer (**Settings → More options**, persisted in `plugins.runtimeLimits`
and `plugins.runtimeOverrides[pluginId]` via `PUT /api/plugins/runtime-limits`).
A per-plugin override can raise a trusted plugin above the global ceiling (up to
4 GiB WASM memory and one year for background work). Viewer routes stay capped at
their route deadlines so browsing and playback remain responsive; offload multi-step
or long-running work to `/ether/job/*` (including `{pending: true, retryInMs, job}`
from kind `/resolve` and `/match`).

## Ten recipes

Commands below run from the repo root. Existing examples are living recipes;
keep their relative SDK imports at the same directory depth, bundle before
shipping, change the reverse-DNS ID before installing a copy alongside its source.
Read the named handler and its manifest together. Run `./ether plugin check DIR`
and `./ether plugin pack DIR` after editing each recipe.

### 1. Catalogue source

```sh
./ether plugin new --kind integration --lang ts ./my-catalogue
```

Or run `./ether plugin new catalogue ./my-catalogue` for a starter that already
returns The Matrix. Replace the generated `/catalog/` branch's empty `metas` with a small bounded
list of `{id:"tt0133093",type:"movie",name:"The Matrix"}`. Keep the listSources
catalog ID (`featured`) aligned with `/catalog/movie/featured.json`. Full typed
catalogue/meta handlers: `sdk/examples/hello/typescript/plugin.ts`.

### 2. A content kind library

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/kind-library sdk/examples/my-library
./ether plugin check sdk/examples/my-library
```

Edit mediaKinds levels, fields, presentation, `library.card` (`poster|landscape|square`), `library.dateDisplay` (`year|date`),
`library.tabs` (up to 50 tabs of `recommended|library|collections|people|view|live`, such as `{key:"live",label:"Live",kind:"live",card:"landscape",searchPlaceholder:"Search live streams"}`, `{key:"topics",label:"Topics",kind:"collections",facet:"topic",order:"name",searchPlaceholder:"Search topics"}`, `{key:"cast",label:"Voice cast",kind:"people",facet:"voiceCast",order:"name",searchPlaceholder:"Search voice cast"}`, or a Smart View History tab `{key:"history",label:"History",kind:"view",layout:"timeline",sort:"lastViewed",direction:"desc",filters:{match:"all",rules:[{field:"viewer",op:"is",value:{history:true}}]}}`),
optional `library.shelves` (up to 40 default Recommended shelves such as `{key:"science-docs",label:"Science documentaries",facet:"topic",values:["Science","Nature"],sort:"released",direction:"desc"}` or multi-facet `filters`),
and `browse.sorts`/`browse.facets` (plus optional `browse.expand: {facets:["tournaments","voiceCast"],ttlHours:168}` for background on-demand `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/expand` slices), then the browse/changes/expand/live/resolve
handlers in `src/plugin.ts` (`onLive` / `OnLive` / `on_live` for live tabs). Keep cursor pages bounded and item IDs stable. Read
[Content kinds](../docs/plugin-kinds.md) before changing resolve or container semantics.

### 3. Resolver / playable source

```sh
./ether plugin new --kind source --lang ts ./my-source
```

Fill `/stream/{type}/{id}.json` with `{streams:[{url:"https://YOUR_HOST/video.mp4"}]}`
using an owner-configured source, not hard-coded credentials. Declare YOUR_HOST
in network permissions if the plugin fetches it. Return lazy stream descriptors
for work that should happen only on a viewer pick. See `sdk/examples/easydebrid`.

### 4. Notification channel

```sh
./ether plugin new --kind notification_channel --lang ts ./my-notifier
```

Implement the notify send and send-test handlers; the generated event handler
shows acknowledgement IDs. Declare webhook hosts and named secrets. Deduplicate
events by ID before sending; a retried outbox delivery must not send twice.

### 5. Page and action

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/movie-night sdk/examples/my-page
./ether plugin check sdk/examples/my-page
```

Edit the ViewSpec and action in `src/plugin.ts`. Keep labels in i18n files and
use stable action IDs. This example saves a shortlist in KV on an explicit pick;
opening a page should read saved data, not repeatedly scan the catalogue.

### 6. Scheduled job

```sh
./ether plugin new job --lang ts ./my-job
```

The job recipe includes `ether.schedule: [{"every":"1h","call":"/ether/refresh"}]` to the manifest
and a handler for that path. The first run happens right after install (within one
scheduler tick once enabled); later runs keep their cadence across server restarts,
including failed attempts. Scheduled calls run off the scheduler pass, never overlap
for the same entry, and may return `{job:"/ether/job/import"}` to hand multi-step
work (for example importing platform game catalogues) to a lowered-priority
continuation job with progress and cancel. Store a cursor/etag in KV (`ether.kv.usage()`
reports `{bytes, keys, quotaBytes, quotaKeys}` including the 256-byte charge per key)
and process a bounded batch per run. Do not create timers in plugin code. Cache
external results; keep the job unconfigured until the owner needs it. Settings
changes must be read each run.

### 7. Settings and setup steps

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/kind-library sdk/examples/my-setup
```

Edit `settings.schema.json`, `contributes.setup.steps`, and `/ether/v1/setup/…/test`
together. Required setup gates library sync until passed or owner-skipped. Use
field-keyed validation errors, never secrets in test responses. The generated
integration template also demonstrates `$ref` settings with translated labels.

### 8. Folder reader

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/local-folders sdk/examples/my-folders
```

Follow `plugin.ts`: ask for a folder setting and `folders:read`, walk only that
root, store an index in KV, and rescan on the owner's action. Owner-selected root
handles are not arbitrary paths. Hash large files with the pollable hash API;
never block a playback request to hash or walk a tree.

### 9. Metadata and artwork

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/hello sdk/examples/my-metadata
```

Use `typescript/plugin.ts`'s meta route (or `go/plugin.go`) as the typed starting
point. Return supported poster/background URLs in metadata. For a canonical
metadata provider add the `metadata` capability and its descriptor from the
reference. **`artwork` is reserved**: do not claim it as a capability. Hosted
requests for images require their hostname in network permissions.

### 10. Stremio-style add-on bridge

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/hello sdk/examples/my-addon
```

The typed hello implementations serve catalog/meta/subtitles routes. A plain
Stremio manifest without `ether` is already supported: install its manifest URL
through Add plugin. If you add native Ether settings/UI, retain the Stremio
fields and set `ether.stremio:true`; Ether derives roles from those resources.
Do not rewrite IDs or response envelopes. Go sidecar from the copied example:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./sdk/examples/my-addon/go/...
# Original runnable sidecar:
CGO_ENABLED=0 go run ./sdk/examples/hello/go/cmd
```

## Fast fixes

| Symptom | Why / exact next step |
|---|---|
| Unknown capability / wrong kind | Check the capability table and change ether.kind or remove the unsupported capability; artwork/ratings are reserved |
| Cannot import module in hosted runtime | Bundle local SDK imports into the entry artifact; no npm resolution in QuickJS |
| `ether` / process / fs unavailable | Use hosted host services, or choose a remote sidecar for OS APIs |
| Permission denied | Declare the exact permission/hostname, reinstall, then have the owner grant it; never retry around revocation |
| Missing settings/strings file | Include the $ref/i18n path inside the package; run check again |
| Empty content library | Complete required setup, enable the plugin, check sync cursors and its mediaKind descriptors |
| Conformance route failed | Read rule + field + route; implement its exact response shape from Reference → Capabilities, then rerun check |
| Dev 401/403 | Set ETHER_TOKEN to the local server's admin token and review its requested grants |
| Dev connection refused | Start your local server and pass its actual --server URL/port |
| Dev install conflicts | Check existing plugin ID/version; do not change identity on every save |
| Labels rejected | Sentence case, length limits, no banned words/punctuation; translate every referenced key |

Before reporting success: review the diff, compile the chosen language, run
conformance, package, and check the visible result on your own development server.
Never claim offline conformance proves playback on a real client. New host
services belong in the generated reference source list and this service map;
regenerate the reference instead of duplicating contracts in prose.

## Slow resolution and remote verification

Kind `/resolve` and `/match` handlers may return `{pending:true,retryInMs:1000}`.
Ether retries after 250–5000 ms (clamped), for at most 25 seconds per Play;
each invocation still has a five-second cap. Pending does not damage health.
If a call is still `pending` after the 25-second wait budget, Ether answers
`503` with `code: "preparing"` and `Retry-After` (from `retryInMs`, or `5` s by
default) on `kind-media`, Vela, Jellyfin and Plex API routes without caching a
negative resolution; only a real empty `sources: []` / `404` answer becomes `409`
`no_source`. For slow searches, also return `job:"/ether/job/prepare"`. Ether
deduplicates running jobs per plugin, kind, item and `partIndex`, passes the
original request body, and uses the existing promoted job deadline and
continuation protocol. A completed
job wakes the resolver before the retry timer. Persist results in KV; never do
work ahead of an actual request. Owner/scheduled jobs (up to 2) and playback
resolver jobs (up to 4) have separate limits per plugin; if all four resolver
slots are busy, Ether returns `503` with `code: "jobs_busy"` and `Retry-After`.

`ether.http.fetch({url,timeoutMs:1200})` and
`ether.http.fetchToCache({url,libraryKey,name,timeoutMs:1200})` bound a slow
remote request (including streaming into cache) by the remaining call deadline.
Hosted code can catch `e.code === "timeout"`. Remote SDK fetches use their local
request context/timeout.

`ether.http.hash({url,algo:"sha256",expectSize:12345})` returns either
`{pending:true,retryInMs:1000}` or `{size,sha256,sha1,md5}`. `expectSize` is
optional; algorithms are `sha256`, `sha1`, `md5`. Hashing streams on the host,
without a blob or guest bytes, through the same network permissions and safe
fetch rules as fetch. It starts only when called. One worker per plugin and
two globally run below playback priority and yield during playback contention.
Disable/uninstall cancels work. Limits: 64 GiB per file, 50 GiB per plugin per
UTC day (including unsuccessful reads), 12 hours per task. The daily cap logs
at Info. Cached digests share one read across algorithms, are private to the
plugin and URL, and include response validators and size. A hit returns
immediately for five minutes; later calls return pending while the host
conditionally revalidates ETag/Last-Modified or streams a new digest. Up to
2048 entries are kept per plugin. Failed tasks may be retried after 30 seconds.
Remote Go uses `RemoteHostClient.Hash`; TypeScript/Python use `http.hash`.

```js
// The manifest must declare the upstream in permissions.network.
function resolve(req) {
  const result = ether.http.hash({url:req.item.hints.url, algo:"sha256"});
  if (result.pending) return {status:200, body:result};
  if (result.sha256 !== req.item.hints.sha256)
    return {status:404, body:{sources:[]}};
  return {status:200, body:{sources:[{pattern:"http",url:req.item.hints.url}]}};
}
// A slow search instead returns pending with job:"/ether/job/prepare";
// that handler writes a KV result and returns {done:true}, or checkpoints with
// {continueInMs:1000,continuation:{cursor:"next"}}. Resolve reads that KV result.
```

## Frontend adapter downloads

Hosted adapters can return a redirect to a host-minted item stream URL (or a
specific zero-based part when an item declares `hints.parts`):

```js
// Whole item (concatenated sequence for multi-part items):
return {status:302, headers:{Location:ether.frontend.streamURL(itemRef).url}};
// Single part (resolves with KindResolveRequest.partIndex = partIndex):
return {status:302, headers:{Location:ether.frontend.streamURL(itemRef, partIndex).url}};
```

In the SDKs, call `streamUrl(ctx, itemRef, partIndex?)` (TypeScript),
`ctx.StreamPartURL(itemRef, partIndex)` (Go), or `ctx.stream_url(item_ref, part_index)`
(Python); an unpinned item ticket also accepts `/ether/v1/kind-media/{ticket}?part=N`.
Multi-file items declare `hints.parts: [{name, mime?, size?, durationSec?}, ...]`
(or a declared `parts` field) so Ether resolves and caches each part with its
zero-based `KindResolveRequest.partIndex`.

Only root-relative local redirect URLs are forwarded. External URLs, authority
changes, control characters, backslashes and known account credential query
parameters are refused. Use the scoped host media ticket, never a login token.

For a cached file or verified archive member, return a blob descriptor instead
of `body` (status 200). The bytes never pass through guest memory:

```js
return {status:200, blob:{
  libraryKey:"pk-my-plugin-firmware", ref:cachedBlobRef, memberIndex:member.index
}};
```

Use the canonical library key returned for your declared media kind. Omit
`memberIndex` to serve the whole blob. The host rechecks enabled state, frontend
capability, ownership, current viewer visibility and the adapter's library list
on every request. It opens only that library's cache namespace and applies the
existing archive safety and runtime limits. The plugin must verify expected
hashes before selecting a cached member; delivery does not assert hash validity.
When trusted metadata provides SHA-1 or MD5 rather than CRC32, call
`ether.archive.extract(cachedBlobRef, member.index)` to stream the member into the
library cache and verify `sha1`/`md5` before serving `{libraryKey, ref: extracted.ref}`.

GET and HEAD are supported. A single GET byte range receives 206; malformed,
multiple or unsatisfiable ranges receive 416. HEAD ignores Range. Downloads use
`application/octet-stream`, a fixed safe attachment filename, no-store and
nosniff; plugin response headers do not override these. Archive range offsets
may require bounded decompression from the start, so do not use this path for
unbounded repeated seeks. Existing JSON `body` responses are unchanged. Remote
HTTP plugins should stream bytes through their existing HTTP response instead;
this descriptor is for the hosted JSON response envelope.

## Recipe: Frontend adapter respecting library Rules

`kinds.items` reads a plugin's raw kind items without evaluating the library's
Rules or viewer visibility. A `frontend_adapter` serving its own protocol
(OPDS, Subsonic, WebDAV, custom clients) must filter through Ether's policy so
items hidden by Rules, hidden libraries, viewer library grants, or viewer
content-safety restrictions never leak to the adapter's clients.

Ether exposes two viewer-scoped host calls that run the exact same
`LibraryPolicy` + `libraryfilter` + viewer-safety checks as the console and
built-in protocol projectors:

- `kinds.browse(kind, query)` — browse or search a kind page with policy already
  applied for the requesting viewer (`{parentId?, level?, cursor?, limit?, sort?, desc?, facets?, query?}`).
  Prefer this when your adapter lists or searches pages directly from Ether's library.
- `kinds.visible(kind, ids)` — check a batch of up to **500** external IDs and
  return only the IDs visible to the requesting viewer, preserving caller order
  and dropping unknown or hidden IDs. Use this when your adapter builds a custom
  list or keeps its own index and needs to prune hidden items before returning them.

**Security guard:** Only viewer-authenticated frontend adapter requests
(`/ether/v1/frontend/*` on a plugin with `frontend_adapter`) may call
`kinds.visible` or `kinds.browse`. Any other route (catalogue browse, jobs,
views, actions, unauthenticated requests) receives a permission error. The
viewer identity always comes from Ether's authenticated request context (and the
host-minted, request-scoped `X-Ether-Viewer-Token` header on remote plugin
callbacks) — never from guest-supplied parameters.

Hosted QuickJS (`plugin.js`):

```js
// Browse/search with Rules and viewer policy already applied:
const page = ether.kinds.browse("comic", { level: "series", limit: 50, query: q });

// Or filter your own candidate IDs in chunks of at most 500:
const allowedIds = ether.kinds.visible("comic", candidateIds.slice(0, 500));
const allowed = new Set(allowedIds);
const visible = candidates.filter((it) => allowed.has(it.id));
```

TypeScript SDK (`@ether/plugin-sdk`, hosted or sidecar):

```ts
import { kindsBrowse, kindsVisible } from "@ether/plugin-sdk";

app.onFrontend("opds", {
  async handle(method, path, _headers, _body, ctx) {
    if (!ctx) return { status: 500, body: "" };
    const page = await kindsBrowse(ctx, "comic", { limit: 50 });
    const visibleIds = await kindsVisible(ctx, "comic", page.items.map((it) => it.id));
    return { status: 200, headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(visibleIds) };
  },
});
```

Go SDK (`sdk/go`):

```go
func (a *adapter) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    pctx, ok := etherplugin.FrontendContext(r.Context())
    if !ok {
        http.Error(w, "missing context", http.StatusForbidden)
        return
    }
    page, err := pctx.KindBrowse("comic", etherplugin.KindBrowseQuery{Limit: 50})
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusForbidden)
        return
    }
    visibleIDs, err := pctx.KindVisible("comic", candidateIDs) // <= 500 IDs per call
    _ = page
    _ = visibleIDs
}
```

Python SDK (`sdk/python`):

```python
class Adapter:
    def handle(self, method, path, headers, body, ctx):
        page = ctx.kinds_browse("comic", {"limit": 50})
        visible_ids = ctx.kinds_visible("comic", candidate_ids[:500])
        return 200, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}, json.dumps({"ids": visible_ids, "count": len(page["items"])})
```



## Source: sdk/catalogue-template/README.md

# Ether catalogue template

Ether reads the official signed plugin marketplace (`https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`, published at `https://braedonsaunders.github.io/ether-plugins/index.json`) by default. To submit a plugin to the official marketplace, upload `<id>-<version>.etherpkg` to a GitHub release, run `ether plugin publish --url <release-asset-url> <dir>` to generate `plugins/<id>.yaml`, and open a pull request against `https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`. Use this template only when operating your own catalogue and setting `plugins.indexUrl` and `plugins.publicKey` together in Ether's configuration.

Set the repository variable `ETHER_REF` to an immutable Ether release tag or commit that includes `ether plugin check` and `ether-release-sign index -check`. The workflow installs both tools from that ref. Set the `ETHER_CATALOGUE_PRIVATE_KEY` and `ETHER_CATALOGUE_PUBLIC_KEY` repository secrets to the base64 Ed25519 signing key and corresponding public key. Keep the private key secret. Pull requests validate without access to signing secrets; pushes to `main` sign and upload `index.json` and `index.json.sig` as a workflow artifact. Publish both files together at the `plugins.indexUrl` configured in Ether.

Add one reviewed YAML file per plugin under `plugins/`; `examples/` contains an illustrative file with placeholder URLs and checksums. Each version must reference a publicly downloadable `.etherpkg` and its SHA-256 digest. CI downloads every non-revoked version, verifies the digest and identity, and runs `ether plugin check` on its unpacked files. The command runs the conformance kit, including copy lint. The index compiler also validates catalogue copy. A revoked entry requires a reason; it is retained in the signed index and its packages are not executed by CI.

Review permissions for each version. A version may override the entry-level permissions using its own `permissions` field. Ether verifies that the package does not request more than the reviewed permissions before marking it verified. Never use the sample values as a real catalogue entry.


## Source: sdk/examples/anime-tosho/README.md

# Anime Tosho

One-click anime indexer plugin for Ether backed by [Anime Tosho NEW](https://animetosho.net).

## What it does

The original Anime Tosho (`animetosho.org`) stopped indexing new releases in May 2026. [Anime Tosho NEW](https://animetosho.net) is a community-funded successor that mirrors anime torrents from Nyaa.si, TokyoTosho, and nekoBT (2017 to present) and exposes open Torznab and Newznab feeds at `https://feed.animetosho.net` with no API key and no account required.

Installing this plugin adds Anime Tosho as an indexer source in Ether with nothing to paste:

- **Torrents and Usenet NZB mirrors:** returns torrent info hashes with public trackers from Torznab, Usenet NZB links from Newznab, or both at once.
- **Anime-aware search:** supports AniDB (`aid`), MyAnimeList (`malid`), Kitsu (`kitsuid`), TMDB (`tmdbid`), TVDB (`tvdbid`), and IMDb (`imdbid`) lookups, absolute episode numbering (such as long-running series like One Piece), and whole-season packs.
- **No API key:** Anime Tosho NEW's Torznab and Newznab feeds are open since v1.3.1, so connection tests and searches work immediately after installation.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Release types** (`releaseTypes`) | `Torrents and NZBs` | Choose whether searches return public torrents, Usenet NZB mirrors, or both. NZB downloads require a Usenet provider configured in Ether. |
| **Category filter** (`category`) | `All categories` | Optional Torznab/Newznab category filter (`5070` for Anime, `2020` for Movies) passed to Anime Tosho NEW. |

## Public torrents notice

Torrents mirrored on Anime Tosho NEW come from public anime trackers such as Nyaa.si and nekoBT. They are **public torrents**, so Ether's private-torrent ratio and H&R rules do not apply to releases from this plugin.

## Credits and polite usage

All feed data, torrent metadata, and Usenet NZB mirrors are provided by [Anime Tosho NEW](https://animetosho.net), a free community-funded project, with ID mappings from AnimeAPI and the Anime Offline Database (ODbL-1.0).

This plugin identifies itself honestly with Ether's User-Agent (`Ether/0.3 (+https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether)`), makes a single bounded feed request per search (`limit=75`), declares conservative indexer rate limits (`120` searches/hour, `1000` searches/day), and propagates upstream `429` / `Retry-After` responses so Ether backs off automatically.

## Development

Rebuild the hosted bundle from `plugin.ts`:

```sh
go run ./sdk/examples/anime-tosho/build
```

Run the plugin conformance check, fixture tests, and Go integration suite:

```sh
ether plugin check ./sdk/examples/anime-tosho
ether plugin test ./sdk/examples/anime-tosho
go test ./sdk/examples/anime-tosho/...
```

## Source: sdk/examples/anime-tosho/plugin.ts

``````
import { plugin, PluginRouteError } from "../../typescript/src/router.ts";
import type { MaybePromise, RawRequest, RawResponse, StreamItem } from "../../typescript/src/types.ts";
import manifest from "./manifest.json";
import schema from "./settings.schema.json";

const API_BASE = "https://feed.animetosho.net";
const USER_AGENT = "Ether/0.3 (+https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether)";
const DEFAULT_LIMIT = 75;
const MAX_XML_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_PARSED_ITEMS = 200;
const MAX_TRACKERS = 8;

export type ReleaseTypes = "both" | "torrents" | "nzbs";

export interface AnimeToshoSettings {
  releaseTypes: ReleaseTypes;
  category: string;
}

export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS: AnimeToshoSettings = {
  releaseTypes: "both",
  category: "",
};

type AnimeToshoStreamItem = StreamItem & {
  nzbUrl?: string;
  sources?: string[];
};

export interface ParsedMediaID {
  mediaType: "movie" | "series";
  prefix: "tt" | "tmdb" | "tvdb" | "anidb" | "mal" | "kitsu";
  id: string;
  season?: number;
  episode?: number;
  isAnimeEntryId: boolean;
}

export interface SearchPlan {
  kind: "movie" | "episode" | "season_pack";
  endpointPath: "/api" | "/api/torznab" | "/api/newznab";
  url: string;
  season?: number;
  episode?: number;
  isAnimeEntryId: boolean;
  categories: string[];
}

export interface FeedItem {
  title: string;
  infoHash: string;
  nzbUrl: string;
  trackers: string[];
  size: number;
  seeders?: number;
  files?: number;
  season?: number;
  episode?: number;
  categories: string[];
}

export interface ParsedFeed {
  items: FeedItem[];
  apiErrorCode?: string;
  apiErrorDescription?: string;
}

const VALID_RELEASE_TYPES = new Set<string>(["both", "torrents", "nzbs"]);
const CATEGORY_LIST_RE = /^\d+(?:,\d+)*$/;
const HEX40_RE = /^[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/;
const BASE32_32_RE = /^[A-Z2-7]{32}$/i;
const VIDEO_EXT_RE = /\.(mkv|mp4|m4v|avi|webm|ts|mov)$/i;
const BASE32_ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567";

export function normalizeSettings(raw: Partial<AnimeToshoSettings> | Record<string, unknown> | undefined): AnimeToshoSettings {
  const releaseTypesRaw = typeof raw?.releaseTypes === "string" ? raw.releaseTypes.trim().toLowerCase() : "";
  const releaseTypes: ReleaseTypes = VALID_RELEASE_TYPES.has(releaseTypesRaw)
    ? (releaseTypesRaw as ReleaseTypes)
    : DEFAULT_SETTINGS.releaseTypes;
  const categoryRaw = typeof raw?.category === "string" ? raw.category.replace(/\s+/g, "") : "";
  const category = categoryRaw && CATEGORY_LIST_RE.test(categoryRaw) ? categoryRaw : "";
  return { releaseTypes, category };
}

export function validateSettings(raw: Partial<AnimeToshoSettings> | Record<string, unknown> | undefined): Record<string, string> {
  const errors: Record<string, string> = {};
  if (raw && raw.releaseTypes !== undefined && raw.releaseTypes !== "") {
    const val = typeof raw.releaseTypes === "string" ? raw.releaseTypes.trim().toLowerCase() : "";
    if (!VALID_RELEASE_TYPES.has(val)) {
      errors["/releaseTypes"] = "Choose torrents, NZBs, or both.";
    }
  }
  if (raw && raw.category !== undefined && raw.category !== "") {
    const val = typeof raw.category === "string" ? raw.category.replace(/\s+/g, "") : "";
    if (!CATEGORY_LIST_RE.test(val)) {
      errors["/category"] = "Choose a valid Torznab or Newznab category.";
    }
  }
  return errors;
}

function parseNonNegInt(raw: string | undefined): number | undefined {
  if (!raw || !/^\d+$/.test(raw)) return undefined;
  const n = Number(raw);
  return Number.isSafeInteger(n) && n >= 0 ? n : undefined;
}

function parsePosInt(raw: string | undefined): number | undefined {
  const n = parseNonNegInt(raw);
  return n !== undefined && n > 0 ? n : undefined;
}

export function parseMediaID(mediaType: string, rawId: string): ParsedMediaID | null {
  if (mediaType !== "movie" && mediaType !== "series") return null;
  const trimmed = (rawId || "").trim();
  if (!trimmed) return null;

  const parts = trimmed.split(":");
  if (parts[0].startsWith("tt")) {
    if (!/^tt\d+$/.test(parts[0])) return null;
    if (mediaType === "movie") {
      if (parts.length !== 1) return null;
      return { mediaType, prefix: "tt", id: parts[0], isAnimeEntryId: false };
    }
    if (parts.length === 2) {
      const season = parseNonNegInt(parts[1]);
      if (season === undefined) return null;
      return { mediaType, prefix: "tt", id: parts[0], season, isAnimeEntryId: false };
    }
    if (parts.length === 3) {
      const season = parseNonNegInt(parts[1]);
      const episode = parsePosInt(parts[2]);
      if (season === undefined || episode === undefined) return null;
      return { mediaType, prefix: "tt", id: parts[0], season, episode, isAnimeEntryId: false };
    }
    return null;
  }

  const prefix = parts[0].toLowerCase();
  if (prefix === "tmdb" || prefix === "tvdb") {
    const numericId = parts[1];
    if (!numericId || !/^\d+$/.test(numericId) || numericId === "0") return null;
    if (mediaType === "movie") {
      if (prefix !== "tmdb" || parts.length !== 2) return null;
      return { mediaType, prefix, id: numericId, isAnimeEntryId: false };
    }
    if (parts.length === 3) {
      const season = parseNonNegInt(parts[2]);
      if (season === undefined) return null;
      return { mediaType, prefix, id: numericId, season, isAnimeEntryId: false };
    }
    if (parts.length === 4) {
      const season = parseNonNegInt(parts[2]);
      const episode = parsePosInt(parts[3]);
      if (season === undefined || episode === undefined) return null;
      return { mediaType, prefix, id: numericId, season, episode, isAnimeEntryId: false };
    }
    return null;
  }

  if (prefix === "anidb" || prefix === "mal" || prefix === "kitsu") {
    const numericId = parts[1];
    if (!numericId || !/^\d+$/.test(numericId) || numericId === "0") return null;
    if (mediaType === "movie") {
      if (parts.length !== 2) return null;
      return { mediaType, prefix, id: numericId, isAnimeEntryId: true };
    }
    if (parts.length === 2) {
      return { mediaType, prefix, id: numericId, isAnimeEntryId: true };
    }
    if (parts.length === 3) {
      const episode = parsePosInt(parts[2]);
      if (episode === undefined) return null;
      return { mediaType, prefix, id: numericId, episode, isAnimeEntryId: true };
    }
    return null;
  }

  return null;
}

function endpointForSettings(settings: AnimeToshoSettings): "/api" | "/api/torznab" | "/api/newznab" {
  if (settings.releaseTypes === "nzbs") return "/api/newznab";
  if (settings.releaseTypes === "torrents") return "/api/torznab";
  return "/api";
}

function buildQueryString(params: Array<[string, string]>): string {
  return params.map(([k, v]) => `${encodeURIComponent(k)}=${encodeURIComponent(v)}`).join("&");
}

function cleanImdbHint(raw: string | undefined): string {
  const s = (raw || "").trim().toLowerCase();
  return /^tt\d+$/.test(s) ? s : "";
}

function cleanNumericHint(raw: string | undefined): string {
  const s = (raw || "").trim();
  return /^\d+$/.test(s) && s !== "0" ? s : "";
}

export function buildSearchPlan(
  mediaType: string,
  rawId: string,
  query: Record<string, string>,
  settings: AnimeToshoSettings,
): SearchPlan | null {
  const parsed = parseMediaID(mediaType, rawId);
  if (!parsed) return null;

  const endpointPath = endpointForSettings(settings);
  const categories = settings.category ? settings.category.split(",").filter(Boolean) : [];
  const params: Array<[string, string]> = [];

  if (parsed.mediaType === "movie") {
    if (parsed.prefix === "anidb") {
      // Anime Tosho NEW caps list aid on t=search rather than t=movie.
      params.push(["t", "search"], ["aid", parsed.id]);
    } else if (parsed.prefix === "mal") {
      params.push(["t", "movie"], ["malid", parsed.id]);
    } else if (parsed.prefix === "kitsu") {
      params.push(["t", "movie"], ["kitsuid", parsed.id]);
    } else {
      const imdbId = parsed.prefix === "tt" ? parsed.id : cleanImdbHint(query.imdbId);
      const tmdbId = parsed.prefix === "tmdb" ? parsed.id : cleanNumericHint(query.tmdbId);
      if (imdbId) {
        params.push(["t", "movie"], ["imdbid", imdbId]);
      } else if (tmdbId) {
        params.push(["t", "movie"], ["tmdbid", tmdbId]);
      } else {
        return null;
      }
    }
    if (categories.length > 0) params.push(["cat", categories.join(",")]);
    params.push(["limit", String(DEFAULT_LIMIT)]);
    return {
      kind: "movie",
      endpointPath,
      url: `${API_BASE}${endpointPath}?${buildQueryString(params)}`,
      isAnimeEntryId: parsed.isAnimeEntryId,
      categories,
    };
  }

  // Series: episode or season pack.
  params.push(["t", "tvsearch"]);

  if (parsed.prefix === "anidb") {
    params.push(["aid", parsed.id]);
  } else if (parsed.prefix === "mal") {
    params.push(["malid", parsed.id]);
  } else if (parsed.prefix === "kitsu") {
    params.push(["kitsuid", parsed.id]);
  } else {
    // Anime Tosho NEW maps multi-season TV series much more reliably by TMDB
    // than by IMDb, so prefer tmdbid when Ether supplies it in the query hints.
    const tmdbId = parsed.prefix === "tmdb" ? parsed.id : cleanNumericHint(query.tmdbId);
    const tvdbId = parsed.prefix === "tvdb" ? parsed.id : "";
    const imdbId = parsed.prefix === "tt" ? parsed.id : cleanImdbHint(query.imdbId);
    if (tmdbId) {
      params.push(["tmdbid", tmdbId]);
    } else if (tvdbId) {
      params.push(["tvdbid", tvdbId]);
    } else if (imdbId) {
      params.push(["imdbid", imdbId]);
    } else {
      return null;
    }
  }

  const querySeason = parseNonNegInt(query.season);
  const hasQuerySeason = querySeason !== undefined;
  const hasQueryEpisode = parsePosInt(query.episode) !== undefined;
  const explicitPack = query.pack === "1" || query.pack === "true";
  const isSeasonPack = parsed.isAnimeEntryId
    ? parsed.episode === undefined || explicitPack
    : parsed.episode === undefined || explicitPack || (hasQuerySeason && !hasQueryEpisode);

  const season = parsed.isAnimeEntryId ? undefined : (parsed.season ?? querySeason);
  const episode = isSeasonPack ? undefined : parsed.episode;

  if (isSeasonPack) {
    if (!parsed.isAnimeEntryId && season !== undefined && season > 0) {
      params.push(["season", String(season)]);
    }
  } else if (episode !== undefined) {
    if (parsed.isAnimeEntryId) {
      params.push(["ep", String(episode)]);
    } else if (season === 1 && episode > 12) {
      // Absolute episode alias (e.g. One Piece :1:1071 or Attack on Titan :1:52):
      // omit season so Anime Tosho matches absolute numbering across seasons.
      params.push(["ep", String(episode)]);
    } else {
      if (season !== undefined) params.push(["season", String(season)]);
      params.push(["ep", String(episode)]);
    }
  }

  if (categories.length > 0) params.push(["cat", categories.join(",")]);
  params.push(["limit", String(DEFAULT_LIMIT)]);

  return {
    kind: isSeasonPack ? "season_pack" : "episode",
    endpointPath,
    url: `${API_BASE}${endpointPath}?${buildQueryString(params)}`,
    season,
    episode,
    isAnimeEntryId: parsed.isAnimeEntryId,
    categories,
  };
}

export function decodeXmlEntities(input: string): string {
  if (!input || !input.includes("&")) return input;
  return input.replace(/&(#x[0-9a-fA-F]+|#\d+|amp|lt|gt|quot|apos);/g, (full, ent: string) => {
    switch (ent) {
      case "amp":
        return "&";
      case "lt":
        return "<";
      case "gt":
        return ">";
      case "quot":
        return '"';
      case "apos":
        return "'";
      default: {
        const code = ent.startsWith("#x") || ent.startsWith("#X")
          ? parseInt(ent.slice(2), 16)
          : parseInt(ent.slice(1), 10);
        if (!Number.isFinite(code) || code <= 0 || code > 0x10ffff) return full;
        try {
          return String.fromCodePoint(code);
        } catch {
          return full;
        }
      }
    }
  });
}

function unwrapCdata(raw: string): string {
  const trimmed = raw.trim();
  if (trimmed.startsWith("<![CDATA[") && trimmed.endsWith("]]>")) {
    return trimmed.slice(9, -3);
  }
  return decodeXmlEntities(trimmed);
}

function parseTagAttributes(tagText: string): Record<string, string> {
  const attrs: Record<string, string> = {};
  const re = /([a-zA-Z0-9_:-]+)\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')/g;
  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
  while ((m = re.exec(tagText)) !== null) {
    attrs[m[1].toLowerCase()] = decodeXmlEntities(m[2] ?? m[3] ?? "");
  }
  return attrs;
}

export function base32ToHex(b32: string): string {
  if (!BASE32_32_RE.test(b32)) return "";
  const upper = b32.toUpperCase();
  let bits = 0;
  let value = 0;
  let out = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < upper.length; i++) {
    const idx = BASE32_ALPHABET.indexOf(upper[i]);
    if (idx < 0) return "";
    value = (value << 5) | idx;
    bits += 5;
    if (bits >= 8) {
      bits -= 8;
      const byte = (value >> bits) & 0xff;
      out += byte.toString(16).padStart(2, "0");
    }
  }
  return out.length === 40 ? out : "";
}

function normalizeInfoHash(raw: string): string {
  const trimmed = (raw || "").trim();
  if (HEX40_RE.test(trimmed)) return trimmed.toLowerCase();
  if (BASE32_32_RE.test(trimmed)) return base32ToHex(trimmed);
  return "";
}

function safeDecodeURI(raw: string): string {
  try {
    return decodeURIComponent(raw.replace(/\+/g, " "));
  } catch {
    return raw;
  }
}

export function parseMagnet(magnetUrl: string): { infoHash: string; trackers: string[] } {
  if (!magnetUrl || !magnetUrl.toLowerCase().startsWith("magnet:?")) {
    return { infoHash: "", trackers: [] };
  }
  let infoHash = "";
  const trackers: string[] = [];
  const seenTrackers = new Set<string>();
  const query = magnetUrl.slice(magnetUrl.indexOf("?") + 1);
  for (const part of query.split("&")) {
    if (!part) continue;
    const eq = part.indexOf("=");
    const key = (eq < 0 ? part : part.slice(0, eq)).toLowerCase();
    const val = eq < 0 ? "" : safeDecodeURI(part.slice(eq + 1)).trim();
    if (key === "xt" && !infoHash) {
      const m = /^urn:btih:([a-zA-Z0-9]+)$/i.exec(val);
      if (m) infoHash = normalizeInfoHash(m[1]);
    } else if (key === "tr" && trackers.length < MAX_TRACKERS) {
      if (/^(https?|udp):\/\/\S+$/i.test(val) && !seenTrackers.has(val)) {
        seenTrackers.add(val);
        trackers.push(val);
      }
    }
  }
  return { infoHash, trackers };
}

function isSafeHttpUrl(raw: string): boolean {
  return /^https?:\/\/[^\s"'<>]+$/i.test(raw.trim());
}

function extractTagContent(block: string, tagName: string): string {
  const open = `<${tagName}`;
  const close = `</${tagName}>`;
  let pos = block.indexOf(open);
  while (pos >= 0) {
    const nextChar = block[pos + open.length];
    if (nextChar === ">" || nextChar === " " || nextChar === "\t" || nextChar === "\n" || nextChar === "\r") {
      const gt = block.indexOf(">", pos + open.length);
      if (gt < 0) return "";
      const end = block.indexOf(close, gt + 1);
      if (end < 0) return "";
      return unwrapCdata(block.slice(gt + 1, end));
    }
    pos = block.indexOf(open, pos + open.length);
  }
  return "";
}

export function parseTorznabFeed(xmlInput: string): ParsedFeed {
  if (!xmlInput) return { items: [] };
  const xml = xmlInput.length > MAX_XML_BYTES ? xmlInput.slice(0, MAX_XML_BYTES) : xmlInput;

  // Check top-level Newznab/Torznab XML error element.
  const errMatch = /<error\b([^>]*?)\/?\s*>/i.exec(xml);
  if (errMatch && !xml.includes("<channel")) {
    const attrs = parseTagAttributes(errMatch[1]);
    return {
      items: [],
      apiErrorCode: attrs.code || "error",
      apiErrorDescription: attrs.description || "Upstream feed error.",
    };
  }

  const items: FeedItem[] = [];
  let cursor = 0;
  while (items.length < MAX_PARSED_ITEMS) {
    const start = xml.indexOf("<item", cursor);
    if (start < 0) break;
    const afterName = xml[start + 5];
    if (afterName !== ">" && afterName !== " " && afterName !== "\t" && afterName !== "\n" && afterName !== "\r") {
      cursor = start + 5;
      continue;
    }
    const startGt = xml.indexOf(">", start + 5);
    if (startGt < 0) break;
    const end = xml.indexOf("</item>", startGt + 1);
    if (end < 0) break;
    cursor = end + 7;

    const block = xml.slice(startGt + 1, end);
    const title = extractTagContent(block, "title").trim();
    if (!title) continue;

    let infoHash = "";
    let nzbUrl = "";
    let magnetUrl = "";
    let size = 0;
    let seeders: number | undefined;
    let files: number | undefined;
    let season: number | undefined;
    let episode: number | undefined;
    const catSet = new Set<string>();

    // Inspect <enclosure .../> tags (may have both torrent and nzb enclosures).
    const encRe = /<enclosure\b([^>]*?)\/?\s*>/gi;
    let encMatch: RegExpExecArray | null;
    while ((encMatch = encRe.exec(block)) !== null) {
      const a = parseTagAttributes(encMatch[1]);
      const type = (a.type || "").toLowerCase();
      const url = (a.url || "").trim();
      const len = parseNonNegInt(a.length);
      if (len && len > size) size = len;
      if (type === "application/x-nzb" && isSafeHttpUrl(url) && !nzbUrl) {
        nzbUrl = url;
      }
    }

    // Inspect <torznab:attr .../> and <newznab:attr .../> tags.
    const attrRe = /<(?:torznab|newznab):attr\b([^>]*?)\/?\s*>/gi;
    let attrMatch: RegExpExecArray | null;
    while ((attrMatch = attrRe.exec(block)) !== null) {
      const a = parseTagAttributes(attrMatch[1]);
      const name = (a.name || "").toLowerCase();
      const value = (a.value || "").trim();
      if (!name || !value) continue;
      switch (name) {
        case "infohash": {
          const h = normalizeInfoHash(value);
          if (h) infoHash = h;
          break;
        }
        case "magneturl":
          if (!magnetUrl) magnetUrl = value;
          break;
        case "nzburl":
          if (isSafeHttpUrl(value)) nzbUrl = value;
          break;
        case "size": {
          const n = parseNonNegInt(value);
          if (n !== undefined && n > 0) size = n;
          break;
        }
        case "seeders": {
          const n = parseNonNegInt(value);
          if (n !== undefined) seeders = n;
          break;
        }
        case "files": {
          const n = parsePosInt(value);
          if (n !== undefined) files = n;
          break;
        }
        case "season": {
          const n = parseNonNegInt(value);
          if (n !== undefined) season = n;
          break;
        }
        case "episode": {
          const n = parsePosInt(value);
          if (n !== undefined) episode = n;
          break;
        }
        case "category":
          if (/^\d+$/.test(value)) catSet.add(value);
          break;
      }
    }

    const magnet = parseMagnet(magnetUrl);
    if (!infoHash && magnet.infoHash) infoHash = magnet.infoHash;

    items.push({
      title,
      infoHash,
      nzbUrl,
      trackers: magnet.trackers,
      size,
      seeders,
      files,
      season,
      episode,
      categories: Array.from(catSet),
    });
  }

  return { items };
}

function formatBytes(bytes: number): string {
  if (!Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes <= 0) return "";
  const units = ["B", "KB", "MB", "GB", "TB"];
  let value = bytes;
  let unit = 0;
  while (value >= 1024 && unit < units.length - 1) {
    value /= 1024;
    unit++;
  }
  return unit === 0 ? `${Math.round(value)} B` : `${value.toFixed(1)} ${units[unit]}`;
}

export function itemsToStreams(
  items: FeedItem[],
  plan: SearchPlan,
  settings: AnimeToshoSettings,
): AnimeToshoStreamItem[] {
  const wantedCats = new Set(plan.categories);
  const ranked: Array<{ tier: number; index: number; item: FeedItem }> = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
    const item = items[i];
    if (wantedCats.size > 0 && item.categories.length > 0) {
      if (!item.categories.some((c) => wantedCats.has(c))) continue;
    }

    let tier = 1;
    if (plan.kind === "season_pack") {
      // Single-episode items carry an explicit episode attribute; exclude them for pack searches.
      if (item.episode !== undefined) continue;
      if (!plan.isAnimeEntryId && plan.season !== undefined && plan.season > 0) {
        if (item.season !== undefined) {
          if (item.season !== plan.season) continue;
          tier = 0;
        }
      }
    } else if (plan.kind === "episode" && !plan.isAnimeEntryId && plan.season !== undefined) {
      if (item.season !== undefined) {
        if (item.season === plan.season) {
          tier = 0;
        } else if (plan.season === 1 && plan.episode !== undefined && plan.episode > 12) {
          // Absolute-episode alias (e.g. :1:52 matching season 3 ep 52): keep behind exact S1 matches.
          tier = 2;
        } else {
          continue;
        }
      }
    }

    ranked.push({ tier, index: i, item });
  }

  ranked.sort((a, b) => (a.tier !== b.tier ? a.tier - b.tier : a.index - b.index));

  const includeTorrents = settings.releaseTypes !== "nzbs";
  const includeNzbs = settings.releaseTypes !== "torrents";
  const seenHashes = new Set<string>();
  const seenNzbs = new Set<string>();
  const streams: AnimeToshoStreamItem[] = [];

  for (const { item } of ranked) {
    const sizeLabel = formatBytes(item.size);
    const behaviorHints: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    if (item.size > 0) behaviorHints.videoSize = item.size;

    if (includeTorrents && item.infoHash && !seenHashes.has(item.infoHash)) {
      seenHashes.add(item.infoHash);
      const details: string[] = [];
      if (item.seeders !== undefined) details.push(`👤 ${item.seeders}`);
      if (sizeLabel) details.push(`💾 ${sizeLabel}`);
      const torrentHints: Record<string, unknown> = { ...behaviorHints };
      if (plan.kind !== "season_pack" && item.files === 1 && VIDEO_EXT_RE.test(item.title)) {
        torrentHints.filename = item.title;
      }
      const stream: AnimeToshoStreamItem = {
        name: "Anime Tosho",
        title: details.length > 0 ? `${item.title}\n${details.join("  ")}` : item.title,
        infoHash: item.infoHash,
      };
      if (item.trackers.length > 0) {
        stream.sources = item.trackers.map((tr) => `tracker:${tr}`);
      }
      if (Object.keys(torrentHints).length > 0) {
        stream.behaviorHints = torrentHints;
      }
      streams.push(stream);
    }

    if (includeNzbs && item.nzbUrl && !seenNzbs.has(item.nzbUrl)) {
      seenNzbs.add(item.nzbUrl);
      const details: string[] = [];
      if (sizeLabel) details.push(`💾 ${sizeLabel}`);
      details.push("Usenet NZB");
      const stream: AnimeToshoStreamItem = {
        name: "Anime Tosho NZB",
        title: `${item.title}\n${details.join(" · ")}`,
        nzbUrl: item.nzbUrl,
      };
      if (Object.keys(behaviorHints).length > 0) {
        stream.behaviorHints = behaviorHints;
      }
      streams.push(stream);
    }
  }

  return streams;
}

function getHeaderCI(headers: Record<string, string> | undefined, name: string): string {
  if (!headers) return "";
  const target = name.toLowerCase();
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(headers)) {
    if (k.toLowerCase() === target) return String(v || "").trim();
  }
  return "";
}

function parseRetryAfter(headers: Record<string, string> | undefined): string {
  const raw = getHeaderCI(headers, "Retry-After");
  return raw || "60";
}

let pendingRetryAfter = "";

const settingsManifest = {
  ...manifest,
  ether: { ...manifest.ether, settings: schema },
} as any;

export const animeTosho = plugin<AnimeToshoSettings>({
  manifest: settingsManifest,
  defaultSettings: DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
  routes: {
    health() {
      return { status: "ok" };
    },

    configure(settings) {
      const errors = validateSettings(settings as unknown as Record<string, unknown>);
      return { errors };
    },

    test(ctx) {
      const res = ctx.ether.http.fetch({
        url: `${API_BASE}/api?t=caps`,
        headers: {
          "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
          Accept: "application/xml, text/xml",
        },
      }) as { status: number; headers?: Record<string, string>; body?: string };

      if (res.status === 429) {
        return { ok: false, message: "Anime Tosho NEW rate limit reached. Try again later." };
      }
      if (res.status !== 200 || !res.body || !res.body.includes("<caps")) {
        return { ok: false, message: "Could not read Anime Tosho NEW feed capabilities." };
      }
      const settings = normalizeSettings(ctx.settings);
      const modeLabel =
        settings.releaseTypes === "torrents"
          ? "Torznab torrents"
          : settings.releaseTypes === "nzbs"
            ? "Newznab Usenet NZBs"
            : "Torznab torrents and Newznab Usenet NZBs";
      return {
        ok: true,
        message: `Connected to Anime Tosho NEW (${modeLabel}).`,
      };
    },

    stream(req, ctx) {
      const settings = normalizeSettings(ctx.settings);
      const mergedQuery: Record<string, string> = { ...req.extra, ...ctx.query };
      const plan = buildSearchPlan(req.type, req.id, mergedQuery, settings);
      if (!plan) {
        return { streams: [] };
      }

      const res = ctx.ether.http.fetch({
        url: plan.url,
        headers: {
          "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
          Accept: "application/xml, text/xml",
        },
      }) as { status: number; headers?: Record<string, string>; body?: string };

      if (res.status === 429 || (res.status === 503 && getHeaderCI(res.headers, "Retry-After"))) {
        pendingRetryAfter = parseRetryAfter(res.headers);
        throw new PluginRouteError(
          429,
          "rate_limited",
          "Anime Tosho NEW rate limit reached. Try again later.",
        );
      }
      if (res.status !== 200) {
        throw new PluginRouteError(
          502,
          "upstream_error",
          `Anime Tosho NEW search failed with HTTP ${res.status}.`,
        );
      }

      const parsed = parseTorznabFeed(res.body || "");
      if (parsed.apiErrorCode) {
        const desc = parsed.apiErrorDescription || "Anime Tosho NEW returned an error.";
        if (parsed.apiErrorCode === "429" || /rate\s*limit|too many requests/i.test(desc)) {
          pendingRetryAfter = parseRetryAfter(res.headers);
          throw new PluginRouteError(429, "rate_limited", desc);
        }
        throw new PluginRouteError(502, "upstream_error", desc);
      }

      return { streams: itemsToStreams(parsed.items, plan, settings) };
    },
  },
});

export function handle(req: RawRequest): MaybePromise<RawResponse> {
  pendingRetryAfter = "";
  const finalize = (res: RawResponse): RawResponse => {
    const retryAfter = pendingRetryAfter;
    pendingRetryAfter = "";
    if (res.status === 429 && retryAfter) {
      return {
        ...res,
        headers: {
          ...(res.headers ?? {}),
          "Retry-After": retryAfter,
        },
      };
    }
    return res;
  };
  const out = animeTosho.handle(req);
  return out instanceof Promise ? out.then(finalize) : finalize(out);
}

if (
  typeof globalThis !== "undefined" &&
  typeof (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).ether === "object" &&
  (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).ether !== null
) {
  (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).handle = handle;
}

``````

## Source: sdk/examples/dub-language/README.md

# Dub language

Adds a release ranking step and a language condition. In Releases, add the step to a profile and enter ISO language codes in preference order. The first matching language wins; MULTi counts for every selected language. Conditions accept an ISO code or list of codes.

Screenshot placeholder: Releases profile drawer showing the ordered audio languages and the step in the ranking ladder.

## Limits

Release names and indexer language tags are imperfect. A language tag does not prove that a track is a dub, and DUB alone does not identify its language. Untagged releases receive no preference. This plugin makes no network calls.

## Source: sdk/examples/dub-language/plugin.ts

``````
import { plugin, type Manifest, type CandidateFacts } from '../../typescript/src/index.ts';
import manifest from './manifest.json' with { type: 'json' };

type Config = { value?: string[] };
const aliases: Record<string,string> = { english:'en', eng:'en', french:'fr', fre:'fr', fra:'fr', german:'de', ger:'de', deu:'de', spanish:'es', spa:'es', italian:'it', ita:'it', japanese:'ja', jpn:'ja', portuguese:'pt', por:'pt', korean:'ko', kor:'ko', chinese:'zh', chi:'zh', zho:'zh', hindi:'hi', hin:'hi' };
// normalize maps a language name, ISO code or regional variant
// ("spanish-latino", "pt-BR") to its two-letter base.
function normalize(s: string): string {
  let v = s.toLowerCase().trim();
  const dash = v.indexOf('-');
  if (dash > 0) v = v.slice(0, dash);
  return aliases[v] || v;
}
// available reads the audio languages Ether parsed from the release name
// and indexer tags. Ether's parser skips title words ("The French
// Dispatch") that a token scan would count, and re-reading the name here
// cost most of the step's time: ranking runs on the hot path, where a
// 500-release batch shares one 50 ms budget.
function available(c: CandidateFacts): Set<string> {
  const langs = new Set<string>();
  const list = c.languages || [];
  for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) langs.add(normalize(list[i]));
  return langs;
}
function speaks(langs: Set<string>, lang: string): boolean {
  const target = normalize(lang);
  return !!target && (langs.has(target) || langs.has('multi'));
}
export const dubPlugin = plugin<Config>({ manifest: manifest as Manifest, routes: {
  rankKey(c, cfg) {
    const wanted = Array.isArray(cfg?.value) ? cfg.value : [];
    if (wanted.length === 0) return 0;
    const langs = available(c);
    for (let i = 0; i < wanted.length; i++) if (speaks(langs, wanted[i])) return wanted.length - i;
    return 0;
  },
  condMatch(c, op, value) {
    if (op === 'equals') return typeof value === 'string' && speaks(available(c), value);
    if (op === 'in') { const values = Array.isArray(value) ? value : typeof value === 'string' ? value.split(',') : []; const langs = available(c); return values.some(v => typeof v === 'string' && speaks(langs, v)); }
    return false;
  }
}});
export const handle = dubPlugin.handle;
export const rank_key = dubPlugin.rank_key;
export const cond_match = dubPlugin.cond_match;

``````

``````
function ok(body:any){return {status:200,body};}
function token(){try{return String(ether.secret.get('apiKey')||'').trim();}catch{return '';}}
function fail(status:number,message:string):never{throw {status,message};}
function api(path:string,body?:any){const key=token();if(!key)fail(401,'Add an EasyDebrid API token in Setup.');const r=ether.http.fetch({url:'https://easydebrid.com/api/v1'+path,method:body?'POST':'GET',headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+key,'Content-Type':'application/json'},...(body?{body:JSON.stringify(body)}:{})});if(r.status<200||r.status>=300)fail(r.status===401||r.status===403?401:r.status===429?429:502,'EasyDebrid request failed (HTTP '+r.status+').');try{return typeof r.body==='string'?JSON.parse(r.body):r.body;}catch{fail(502,'EasyDebrid returned invalid JSON.');}}
function magnet(h:string){if(!/^[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/.test(h))fail(400,'A valid torrent info hash is required.');return 'magnet:?xt=urn:btih:'+h.toLowerCase();}
function files(hash:string){const result=api('/link/generate',{url:magnet(hash)});if(!Array.isArray(result.files))fail(502,'EasyDebrid returned no file list.');return result.files.map((f:any)=>{const path=[...(Array.isArray(f.directory)?f.directory:[]),f.filename].filter(Boolean).join('/');return {id:path,path,size:Number(f.size)||0,link:String(f.url||'')};}).filter((f:any)=>f.path&&f.size>0);}
function account(){const a=api('/user/details');const day=String(a.paid_until||'');const end=/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(day)?day+'T23:59:59Z':day;const ms=Date.parse(end);return {user:String(a.id||''),premium:Number.isFinite(ms)&&ms>Date.now(),...(Number.isFinite(ms)?{expires:new Date(ms).toISOString()}:{})};}
export function handle(req:any){try{
 if(req.path==='/ether/configure')return ok({errors:{}});
 if(req.path==='/ether/health')return ok({status:token()?'ok':'attention',reason:token()?'':'Add an EasyDebrid API token in Setup.'});
 if(req.path==='/ether/test'||req.path==='/ether/action/test'){const a=account();const message=a.premium?'EasyDebrid account connected; premium access is active.':'Account connected, but premium access is expired or unavailable.';return ok(req.path==='/ether/test'?{ok:a.premium,message}:{toast:message,refresh:true});}
 if(req.path==='/ether/view/account')return ok({title:'EasyDebrid',spec:{specVersion:1,layout:'detail',header:[{kind:'page-header',title:{$:'title'},description:{$:'subtitle'}}],body:[{kind:'stat-tile',iconKey:'key',accent:'primary',label:'$t:state',value:{$:'state'}},{kind:'panel',title:'$t:connection',blocks:[{kind:'widget',widget:'ether.actionButton',props:{label:'$t:test',action:'test'}}]},{kind:'panel',title:'$t:capabilities',blocks:[{kind:'text',content:'$t:help'},{kind:'text',content:'$t:docs'}]}]},data:{title:'EasyDebrid',subtitle:'A native plugin source in Sources → Debrid. Configure your account in Plugins → EasyDebrid → Setup, then run the connection test.',state:token()?'Token saved; test account':'Setup required'}});
 if(req.path==='/ether/debrid/account')return ok(account());
 if(req.path==='/ether/debrid/find'||req.path==='/ether/debrid/remove')return {status:501,body:{error:{code:'unsupported',message:'Cached-only provider; no account torrent queue.'}}};
 if(req.path==='/ether/debrid/check'){
  const hashes=Array.isArray(req.body?.hashes)?req.body.hashes:[];if(hashes.length>10000)fail(400,'Too many hashes.');const cached:any={};
  for(let n=0;n<hashes.length;n+=100){const batch=hashes.slice(n,n+100);const r=api('/link/lookup',{urls:batch.map(magnet)});if(!Array.isArray(r.cached)||r.cached.length!==batch.length)fail(502,'EasyDebrid returned an invalid cache check.');batch.forEach((h:string,i:number)=>cached[h]=r.cached[i]===true);}return ok({cached});
 }
 if(req.path==='/ether/debrid/acquire'){const h=String(req.body?.infoHash||'');const r=api('/link/lookup',{urls:[magnet(h)]});if(r.cached?.[0]!==true)return {status:409,body:{error:{code:'not_cached',message:'This torrent is not cached.'}}};return ok({torrentId:h,ready:true,added:false,files:files(h)});}
 if(req.path==='/ether/debrid/link'){const h=String(req.body?.infoHash||req.body?.torrentId||'');const f=files(h).find((f:any)=>f.path===req.body?.path);if(!f)fail(404,'The selected file is no longer available.');return ok({url:f.link,size:f.size});}
 return {status:404,body:{error:{code:'not_found',message:'Route not found.'}}};
 }catch(e){const status=Number(e.status)||502,message=e.status?e.message:'EasyDebrid could not be reached.';if(req.path==='/ether/test')return ok({ok:false,message});return {status,body:{error:{code:'provider_error',message}}};}}
(globalThis as any).handle=handle;

``````

## Source: sdk/examples/english-dubs/README.md

# English dubbed anime

First-party Ether plugin that exposes anime series and films with an English dub as ready-made list sources for Home rows, smart collections, and library rules.

## What it provides

- **Anime with an English dub (`dubbed`)** — TV series and films confirmed to have an English dub in the community MAL-Dubs dataset.
- **Dub in progress (`incomplete`)** — TV series and films whose English dub is still being released.
- **Status page** — Displays cached mapped series, movie, and in-progress counts with a manual cache refresh action.

## How it works

The plugin fetches both upstream datasets at runtime and does not bundle any copy of the data:

1. **Dub status list:** [MAL-Dubs](https://github.com/MAL-Dubs/MAL-Dubs) (`data/dubInfo.json`, ~5,700 MyAnimeList IDs across `dubbed` and `incomplete`).
2. **ID mapping:** [Fribb/anime-lists](https://github.com/Fribb/anime-lists) (`anime-list-mini.json`), used at runtime to map MyAnimeList IDs to TMDB IDs (with IMDb and TVDB fallbacks where a TMDB ID is absent) because Ether's list source resolver matches canonical IMDb, TMDB, and TVDB identities.

Both files are cached in plugin KV storage in compacted form and refreshed daily via a scheduled job (`/ether/job/refresh`) using conditional HTTP requests (`ETag` / `If-None-Match` and `Last-Modified` / `If-Modified-Since`). If an upstream refresh fails transiently after the cache is populated, the plugin serves the previously cached index.

## Settings

| Setting | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Include incomplete dubs (`includeIncomplete`) | Boolean | `false` | Merges entries from the `incomplete` array into the main **Anime with an English dub** list (deduplicated by title). |
| Type filter (`typeFilter`) | Select (`both`, `series`, `movies`) | `both` | Restricts catalog responses to anime series, anime movies, or both. |

## Permissions

- **Network (`raw.githubusercontent.com`)** — Used only to fetch `MAL-Dubs/MAL-Dubs` (`data/dubInfo.json`) and `Fribb/anime-lists` (`anime-list-mini.json`).

## Credits and licenses

- Plugin source code: MIT License.
- Dub list data: [MAL-Dubs](https://github.com/MAL-Dubs/MAL-Dubs), licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)](https://github.com/MAL-Dubs/MAL-Dubs/blob/main/LICENSE). No copy of the MAL-Dubs data is bundled with this plugin; it is fetched directly at runtime by each server.
- Anime ID mapping: [Fribb/anime-lists](https://github.com/Fribb/anime-lists).

## Limits

- **Community-maintained data:** Dub coverage and completeness depend on volunteer updates to MAL-Dubs; newly announced simuldubs or recent releases may lag behind broadcast dates.
- **MAL-to-TMDB mapping gaps:** Not every MyAnimeList entry (especially OVAs, specials, and newer titles) has a TMDB, TVDB, or IMDb mapping in `Fribb/anime-lists`. Unmapped entries cannot be matched to Ether's canonical catalogue and are omitted.
- **Season collapsing:** MyAnimeList assigns separate IDs per season or cour, while TMDB groups seasons under one show. Duplicate TMDB show IDs are collapsed into a single show entry, so a show appears once if at least one of its seasons is listed as dubbed.
- **Collection item limit:** Ether bounds each collection or Home row list source read to at most 2,000 items per refresh. The confirmed dubbed series list currently exceeds 2,000 TMDB shows, so full mixed or series-only collections receive the first 2,000 mapped items in source order.

## Verification

From the repository root:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o ./ether ./cmd/ether
./ether plugin check sdk/examples/english-dubs
./ether plugin test sdk/examples/english-dubs
./ether plugin pack -o ./english-dubs.etherpkg sdk/examples/english-dubs
./ether plugin check ./english-dubs.etherpkg
node --test sdk/examples/english-dubs/tests/plugin.test.ts
```
