## Source: sdk/go/tunnel.go#*Plugin.DispatchTunnelFrame

``````
// DispatchTunnelFrame executes a `"request"` TunnelFrame against a Plugin and
// returns the outgoing response frames (either a single `"response"` frame or a
// `"response_start"` / `"response_chunk"` / `"response_end"` sequence for
// `/ether/file/*` binary responses).
func (p *Plugin) DispatchTunnelFrame(ctx context.Context, frame TunnelFrame, maxChunkBytes int) []TunnelFrame {
	if frame.Type != "request" || frame.ID == "" {
		return nil
	}
	if maxChunkBytes <= 0 {
		maxChunkBytes = DefaultMaxChunkBytes
	}

	var decodedBody []byte
	if frame.Body != "" {
		b, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(frame.Body)
		if err != nil {
			return []TunnelFrame{{
				Type:  "error",
				ID:    frame.ID,
				Error: &TunnelError{Code: "bad_request", Message: "Invalid base64 request body."},
			}}
		}
		decodedBody = b
	}

	hdrs := map[string]string{}
	for k, vals := range frame.Headers {
		if len(vals) > 0 {
			hdrs[k] = vals[0]
		}
	}
	if frame.RequestID != "" && hdrs["X-Ether-Request-ID"] == "" {
		hdrs["X-Ether-Request-ID"] = frame.RequestID
	}
	query := map[string]string{}
	for k, vals := range frame.Query {
		if len(vals) > 0 {
			query[k] = vals[0]
		}
	}

	res := p.Dispatch(ctx, RawRequest{
		Method:  frame.Method,
		Path:    frame.Path,
		Query:   query,
		Headers: hdrs,
		Body:    decodedBody,
	})

	multiHeaders := map[string][]string{}
	for k, v := range res.Headers {
		multiHeaders[k] = []string{v}
	}

	if res.BinaryBody != nil && strings.HasPrefix(frame.Path, "/ether/file/") {
		out := []TunnelFrame{{
			Type:    "response_start",
			ID:      frame.ID,
			Status:  res.Status,
			Headers: multiHeaders,
		}}
		limit := maxChunkBytes
		if limit < 1024 {
			limit = 1024
		}
		for offset := 0; offset < len(res.BinaryBody); offset += limit {
			end := offset + limit
			if end > len(res.BinaryBody) {
				end = len(res.BinaryBody)
			}
			out = append(out, TunnelFrame{
				Type: "response_chunk",
				ID:   frame.ID,
				Data: base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(res.BinaryBody[offset:end]),
			})
		}
		out = append(out, TunnelFrame{
			Type: "response_end",
			ID:   frame.ID,
		})
		return out
	}

	payload := res.Body
	if res.BinaryBody != nil {
		payload = res.BinaryBody
	}
	var encodedBody string
	if len(payload) > 0 {
		encodedBody = base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(payload)
	}
	return []TunnelFrame{{
		Type:    "response",
		ID:      frame.ID,
		Status:  res.Status,
		Headers: multiHeaders,
		Body:    encodedBody,
	}}
}
``````

## Source: sdk/go/tunnel.go#*Plugin.startTunnel

``````
func (p *Plugin) startTunnel(ctx context.Context, tunnelURL, credential string, fromFile bool, stateDir string) (*ServeHandle, error) {
	if tunnelURL == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("tunnel mode requires TunnelURL or ETHER_TUNNEL_URL")
	}
	loopCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	conn, maxChunk, err := p.dialTunnel(loopCtx, tunnelURL, credential)
	if err != nil {
		cancel()
		if errors.Is(err, errUnauthorized) && fromFile {
			clearSavedCredential(p.manifest.ID, stateDir)
			return nil, noCredentialError()
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		defer cancel()
		backoff := 100 * time.Millisecond
		for {
			started := time.Now()
			p.runTunnel(loopCtx, conn, maxChunk)
			if time.Since(started) >= time.Minute {
				backoff = 100 * time.Millisecond
			}
			for {
				// Equal jitter keeps retries bounded and avoids synchronized sidecars.
				delay := backoff/2 + time.Duration(rand.Int64N(int64(backoff/2)))
				timer := time.NewTimer(delay)
				select {
				case <-loopCtx.Done():
					timer.Stop()
					return
				case <-timer.C:
				}
				if backoff < 10*time.Second {
					backoff = min(backoff*2, 10*time.Second)
				}
				conn, maxChunk, err = p.dialTunnel(loopCtx, tunnelURL, credential)
				if err == nil {
					break
				}
				// A saved credential the server no longer accepts is dead:
				// clear it and stop rather than reconnect with it forever.
				if errors.Is(err, errUnauthorized) && fromFile {
					clearSavedCredential(p.manifest.ID, stateDir)
					return
				}
			}
		}
	}()
	return &ServeHandle{
		Done: done,
		Mode: "tunnel",
		URL:  tunnelURL,
		Close: func() error {
			cancel()
			<-done
			return nil
		},
	}, nil
}
``````

## Source: sdk/go/tunnel.go#*Plugin.dialTunnel

``````
// dialTunnel authenticates and completes the handshake on every attempt.
// Its timeout also bounds a peer that accepts a socket but never welcomes us.
func (p *Plugin) dialTunnel(ctx context.Context, tunnelURL, credential string) (*websocket.Conn, int, error) {
	handshakeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	dialOpts := &websocket.DialOptions{
		Subprotocols: []string{TunnelProtocol},
		HTTPHeader:   http.Header{},
	}
	if credential != "" {
		dialOpts.HTTPHeader.Set("X-Ether-Plugin-Credential", credential)
	}
	conn, resp, err := websocket.Dial(handshakeCtx, tunnelURL, dialOpts)
	if err != nil {
		if resp != nil {
			if resp.Body != nil {
				resp.Body.Close()
			}
			if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusUnauthorized {
				return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w (HTTP %d)", errUnauthorized, resp.StatusCode)
			}
		}
		return nil, 0, err
	}
	conn.SetReadLimit(16 << 20)
	helloBytes, _ := json.Marshal(TunnelFrame{
		Type: "hello", Protocol: TunnelProtocol, Plugin: p.manifest.ID,
		Features: []string{"range", "stream"},
	})
	if err := conn.Write(handshakeCtx, websocket.MessageText, helloBytes); err != nil {
		conn.CloseNow()
		return nil, 0, err
	}
	_, welcomeBytes, err := conn.Read(handshakeCtx)
	if err != nil {
		conn.CloseNow()
		return nil, 0, err
	}
	var welcome TunnelFrame
	if err := json.Unmarshal(welcomeBytes, &welcome); err != nil || welcome.Type != "welcome" {
		conn.CloseNow()
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("unexpected tunnel handshake response: %s", string(welcomeBytes))
	}
	maxChunk := welcome.MaxChunkBytes
	if maxChunk <= 0 {
		maxChunk = DefaultMaxChunkBytes
	}
	return conn, maxChunk, nil
}
``````

## Source: sdk/go/tunnel.go#*Plugin.runTunnel

``````
// runTunnel owns one socket. Only the supervisor dials; old handlers retain
// their old socket and are cancelled before a replacement is opened.
func (p *Plugin) runTunnel(ctx context.Context, conn *websocket.Conn, maxChunk int) {
	loopCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	defer conn.CloseNow()
	var mu sync.Mutex
	active := make(map[string]context.CancelFunc)
	defer func() {
		mu.Lock()
		defer mu.Unlock()
		for _, stop := range active {
			stop()
		}
	}()
	for {
		_, msgBytes, err := conn.Read(loopCtx)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		var frame TunnelFrame
		if json.Unmarshal(msgBytes, &frame) != nil {
			continue
		}
		if frame.Type == "cancel" {
			mu.Lock()
			stop := active[frame.ID]
			mu.Unlock()
			if stop != nil {
				stop()
			}
			continue
		}
		if frame.Type != "request" {
			continue
		}
		requestCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(loopCtx)
		mu.Lock()
		active[frame.ID] = stop
		mu.Unlock()
		go func(frame TunnelFrame) {
			defer func() { mu.Lock(); delete(active, frame.ID); mu.Unlock(); stop() }()
			for _, reply := range p.DispatchTunnelFrame(requestCtx, frame, maxChunk) {
				if requestCtx.Err() != nil {
					return
				}
				b, err := json.Marshal(reply)
				if err != nil {
					return
				}
				// WebSocket cancellation is connection-fatal. A per-request cancel
				// must stop dispatch, never interrupt a write on the shared socket.
				writeCtx, writeCancel := context.WithTimeout(loopCtx, 10*time.Second)
				err = conn.Write(writeCtx, websocket.MessageText, b)
				writeCancel()
				if err != nil {
					cancel()
					return
				}
			}
		}(frame)
	}
}
``````

## Source: sdk/go/types.go#EtherManifestBlock

``````
// EtherManifestBlock holds the EPP/1 `ether` manifest block.
type EtherManifestBlock struct {
	Protocol     int             `json:"protocol"`

	} `json:"stremio,omitempty"`

## Source: sdk/go/types.go#KindLibraryTab

``````
// KindLibraryTab declares one sub-tab shown inside a plugin library.
type KindLibraryTab struct {
	Key               string                `json:"key"`
	Label             string                `json:"label"`
	Kind              string                `json:"kind"`                        // recommended|library|collections|people|view|live
	Facet             string                `json:"facet,omitempty"`             // declared browse.facets entry (optional on collections; required people-type facet on people)
	Order             string                `json:"order,omitempty"`             // count|name (default count on collections, name on people)
	Card              string                `json:"card,omitempty"`              // landscape (default)|poster|square (live tabs only)
	Layout            string                `json:"layout,omitempty"`            // grid (default)|list|timeline (view tabs only)
	Search            *bool                 `json:"search,omitempty"`            // collections/people/view/live only; default true
	SearchPlaceholder string                `json:"searchPlaceholder,omitempty"` // localizable placeholder (<=60 chars; collections/people/view/live when search is enabled)
	Sort              string                `json:"sort,omitempty"`              // one of browse.sorts or lastViewed (facet collections or view)
	Direction         string                `json:"direction,omitempty"`         // asc|desc (facet collections or view)
	Filters           *KindLibraryTabFilter `json:"filters,omitempty"`           // saved filter rules (view tabs only)
}
``````

## Source: sdk/python/README.md

# `ether_plugin` (Python SDK)

Single-file, standard-library-only Python 3.9+ SDK for Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1).

## Features

- Zero external pip dependencies (`http.server`, `urllib.request`, `json`, `socket`, `base64`).
- Same declarative `plugin(manifest=..., routes=...)` router shape as `@ether/plugin-sdk` and `sdk/go`.
- Runs as an HTTP sidecar (`serve(p, mode="http")`) or an outbound WebSocket tunnel sidecar (`serve(p, mode="tunnel")`).
- Supports Ether Flows custom events (`ctx.ether.events.publish(key, payload, correlation)` -> `POST /ether/plugin-host/events/publish`) and Flow actions (`routes={"flow_action": ...}` with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` and `dryRun`).
- Includes `RemoteHostClient` for `/ether/plugin-host/*` authenticated with `X-Ether-Plugin-Credential`, plus `create_test_harness`, `create_mock_host_client`, `fixtures`, and starter capability templates.

## Usage

```python
from ether_plugin import plugin, serve

hello = plugin(
    manifest={
        "id": "org.ether.examples.hello",
        "name": "Hello plugin",
        "version": "0.1.0",
        "description": "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
        "types": ["movie"],
        "idPrefixes": ["tt"],
        "catalogs": [{"type": "movie", "id": "hello", "name": "Hello movies"}],
        "resources": ["catalog", "meta"],
        "ether": {
            "protocol": 1,
            "kind": "extension",
            "capabilities": ["list_source", "ui"],
            "summary": "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
            "runtime": {"kind": "remote"},
        },
    },
    routes={
        "catalog": lambda req, ctx: {
            "metas": [
                {
                    "id": "tt0133093",
                    "type": req["type"],
                    "name": f"Hello from {req['id']}",
                    "releaseInfo": "1999",
                }
            ]
        },
    },
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(hello, background=False)
```

Tunnel mode makes one connection and returns when it drops. Use a process
supervisor to restart the sidecar after a disconnection.

## Sidecars

A sidecar is a remote plugin whose program runs on a machine you choose and
dials out to Ether over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket, so it needs no inbound
port. Pair once and the SDK saves the credential:

```sh
ETHER_URL=https://ether.example.com \
ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data \
ETHER_PAIRING_CODE=PAIR-1234 \
python3 plugin.py
```

Create the code in Ether under Plugins › your plugin › Connect a sidecar; it is
valid for 5 minutes and single use. `serve(plugin, mode="tunnel")` resolves the
credential in this order: an explicit credential, then the saved file, then the
pairing code (exchanged once and saved). With none it raises `CredentialError`
with one clear line.

- `ETHER_URL` — the server's `http(s)` base; the pair and `ws(s)` tunnel URLs
  are derived from it.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_CREDENTIAL` — an explicit credential; always wins.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` — where the credential is saved, else `/data` when it
  exists and is writable (a Docker volume), else `~/.config/ether-plugins/<id>/`.
- `ETHER_PAIRING_CODE` — a one-time code.

The credential is saved at `<state dir>/credential` (mode `0600`, directory
`0700`). If the tunnel rejects a saved credential, the file is deleted and
`serve` raises `CredentialError` instead of reconnecting forever.

A Dockerfile that keeps the credential across restarts:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY plugin.py ether_plugin.py manifest.json settings.schema.json ./
VOLUME /data
ENV ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data
CMD ["python3", "plugin.py"]
```

Declare how the console runs it with an `ether.sidecar` manifest block:

```json
"ether": {
  "runtime": { "kind": "remote" },
  "sidecar": {
    "command": "python3 plugin.py",
    "docs": "https://example.com/my-sidecar"
  }
}
```

`docker` is an image reference; `download` (an https URL) with `command` (a
single line) is the alternative; `docs` adds a setup link.


Content-kind item dictionaries may include `unavailable: {"code": "no_verified_source",
"detail": "No verified source"}`. Ether keeps these items visible with the reason
and refuses resolution until a later upsert omits the field. `pattern: "file"`
with a `path` is reserved for hosted resolvers with `folders: read`; Python
sidecars cannot access host files or call `folders.hash`. See `docs/plugin-kinds.md`.

### Continuing background jobs

A `job` handler receives `{"name": ..., "continuation": ...}`. Return
`{"continueInMs": 0, "continuation": {"next": 41}, "progress": "Platform 41 of 92"}`
to continue. Return `{"done": True}` or `{"failed": "reason"}` to finish; an
absent `continueInMs` also finishes. Store durable checkpoints in KV to recover
on a later owner-started run after restart. Tokens are at most 64 KiB and progress
at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes. The drawer supports progress and cancellation.

Ether uses owner-controlled global/per-plugin ceilings under Plugins: default
2 GiB memory (up to wasm32 4 GiB), 12 hours, effectively unlimited background
compute, up to 4 hosted WASM instances (`poolSize`, default 2; background jobs
hold at most `poolSize - 1`), 8 GiB downloads/member expansion, 32 GiB total
expansion and 65,535 ZIP members. Downloads also obey library cache quotas.
Hosted manifests request `ether.runtime.limits` with `memoryBytes`, `deadline`,
`unitBudget`, `poolSize`, `fetchBytes`, `archiveMemberBytes`,
`archiveExpandedBytes` and `archiveMembers`. Install preview
and detail show requested and granted values. Jobs pause during playback/high
host load and use low CPU/IO priority. A 1,000,000-call sanity bound applies;
viewer browse/search/resolve/playback calls retain tight time and compute budgets.
Remote Python processes manage their own CPU/memory. See the TypeScript SDK
README for route classification, policy APIs and complete job behavior.


## Source: sdk/python/ether_plugin.py

``````
"""Ether Plugin SDK for Python 3.9+ (stdlib-only, zero external dependencies).

Implements Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1) for sidecar and remote plugins:
- Declarative router (`plugin(manifest=..., routes=...)`) with identical route
  semantics to `@ether/plugin-sdk` and `sdk/go`.
- Settings schema decoding, validation, and copy-rule linting (SPEC §5.5).
- Localization helper (`create_i18n`, `t_ref`).
- Remote host client (`RemoteHostClient`) for `/ether/plugin-host/*` authenticated
  with `X-Ether-Plugin-Credential` (SPEC §5.1.5, WS8b).
- HTTP sidecar server (`serve(..., mode="http")`) and WebSocket tunnel client
  (`serve(..., mode="tunnel")`, `dispatch_over_tunnel_frame`).
- Local test harness, mock host client, fixtures, and capability starter templates.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import http.server
import inspect
import json
import logging
import os
import re
import socket
import socketserver
import ssl
import struct
import threading
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Literal, Optional, Tuple, TypedDict, Union

TUNNEL_PROTOCOL = "ether-tunnel-v1"
DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 64 * 1024
MAX_KIND_VISIBLE_IDS = 500
HEADER_VIEWER_TOKEN = "X-Ether-Viewer-Token"
HEADER_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY = "X-Ether-Idempotency-Key"

ALLOWED_SETTING_KINDS = frozenset(
    {
        "group",
        "text",
        "secret",
        "duration",
        "readonly",
        "number",
        "bool",
        "select",
        "list",
        "bytes",
        "hidden",
        "multiSelect",
        "orderedList",
        "language",
        "viewer",
        "collection",
        "folder",
        "url",
        "title",
    }
)

_BANNED_COPY_RE = re.compile(r"\b(simply|easily|just)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
_INTERP_RE = re.compile(r"\{([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\}")


class PluginHttpError(Exception):
    """Structured HTTP error raised by a plugin route handler."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = int(status)
        self.code = str(code)
        self.message = str(message)


PluginRouteError = PluginHttpError


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Copy rules & i18n helpers (SPEC §2.7, §2.8, §5.1.1, §5.6)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def t_ref(key: str) -> str:
    """Returns a `$t:<key>` reference for manifest and ViewSpec fields."""
    return f"$t:{key}"


def lint_copy(raw: str, max_len: int = 0) -> str:
    """Validates a user-visible string against Ether's copy rules."""
    s = raw.strip()
    if max_len > 0 and len(s) > max_len:
        return f"is longer than {max_len} characters"
    if "—" in s or "–" in s:
        return "must not contain em or en dashes"
    if "!" in s:
        return "must not contain exclamation marks"
    if _BANNED_COPY_RE.search(s):
        return "must not use the words simply, just or easily"
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha():
            if ch.islower():
                return "must use sentence case"
            break
    words = [w for w in s.split() if w]
    if len(words) >= 3:
        caps = sum(1 for w in words if w[0].isalpha() and w[0].isupper())
        if caps * 3 > len(words) * 2:
            return "must use sentence case"
    return ""


class I18nHelper:
    """Resolves localized strings with fallback to base language and 'en'."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        strings: Optional[Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]] = None,
        default_locale: str = "en",
    ) -> None:
        self._strings: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = strings or {}
        self._default_locale = default_locale or "en"

    def t(
        self,
        raw_key: str,
        params: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        locale: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> str:
        key = raw_key[3:] if raw_key.startswith("$t:") else raw_key
        loc = locale or self._default_locale
        base = loc.split("-")[0] if loc else ""
        template: Optional[str] = None
        for candidate in (loc, base, "en"):
            if not candidate:
                continue
            table = self._strings.get(candidate)
            if table and key in table:
                template = table[key]
                break
        if template is None:
            template = key
        if not params:
            return template

        def _replace(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
            name = match.group(1)
            return str(params[name]) if name in params else match.group(0)

        return _INTERP_RE.sub(_replace, template)

    def ref(self, key: str) -> str:
        return t_ref(key)

    def catalog(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:
        return self._strings


def create_i18n(
    strings: Optional[Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]] = None,
    default_locale: str = "en",
) -> I18nHelper:
    return I18nHelper(strings=strings, default_locale=default_locale)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Settings schema decoding and linting (SPEC §5.5)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def collect_setting_fields(schema: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        return []
    out: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    def _walk(node: Any) -> None:
        if isinstance(node, list):
            for item in node:
                _walk(item)
            return
        if not isinstance(node, dict):
            return
        key = (
            node.get("key")
            or node.get("name")
            or node.get("id")
            or node.get("field")
            or ""
        )
        kind = node.get("kind", "")
        if isinstance(key, str) and key and isinstance(kind, str) and kind and kind != "group":
            out.append(
                {
                    "key": key,
                    "kind": kind,
                    "label": node.get("label"),
                    "hint": node.get("hint"),
                    "required": node.get("required") is True,
                    "default": node.get("default"),
                    "min": node.get("min"),
                    "max": node.get("max"),
                }
            )
        for v in node.values():
            if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
                _walk(v)

    _walk(schema)
    return out


def lint_settings_schema(schema: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        return []
    problems: List[Dict[str, str]] = []

    def _walk(node: Any, path: str) -> None:
        if isinstance(node, list):
            for idx, item in enumerate(node):
                _walk(item, f"{path}[{idx}]")
            return
        if not isinstance(node, dict):
            return
        kind = node.get("kind")
        if isinstance(kind, str):
            if kind == "json":
                problems.append(
                    {
                        "field": f"{path}.kind",
                        "message": "the json field kind is not allowed in plugin settings",
                    }
                )
            elif kind not in ALLOWED_SETTING_KINDS:
                problems.append(
                    {
                        "field": f"{path}.kind",
                        "message": f'unknown field kind "{kind}"',
                    }
                )
        label = node.get("label")
        if isinstance(label, str) and not label.startswith("$t:"):
            msg = lint_copy(label, 40)
            if msg:
                problems.append({"field": f"{path}.label", "message": msg})
        hint = node.get("hint")
        if isinstance(hint, str) and not hint.startswith("$t:"):
            msg = lint_copy(hint, 120)
            if msg:
                problems.append({"field": f"{path}.hint", "message": msg})
            trimmed = hint.rstrip(".")
            if "." in trimmed:
                problems.append({"field": f"{path}.hint", "message": "must be one sentence"})
        for k, v in node.items():
            if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
                _walk(v, f"{path}.{k}")

    _walk(schema, "ether.settings")
    return problems


def decode_settings(
    schema: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
    incoming: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    defaults: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Dict[str, str]]:
    fields = collect_setting_fields(schema)
    result: Dict[str, Any] = dict(defaults or {})
    errors: Dict[str, str] = {}

    for f in fields:
        if f.get("default") is not None and f["key"] not in result:
            result[f["key"]] = f["default"]

    if isinstance(incoming, dict):
        for k, v in incoming.items():
            result[k] = v

    for f in fields:
        key = f["key"]
        kind = f["kind"]
        val = result.get(key)
        ptr = f"/{key}"
        if f.get("required") and (val is None or val == ""):
            errors[ptr] = "is required"
            continue
        if val is None or val == "":
            continue
        if kind in ("number", "bytes", "viewer"):
            if isinstance(val, bool):
                errors[ptr] = "must be a number"
                continue
            try:
                num = float(val) if isinstance(val, str) and "." in val else int(val) if isinstance(val, (int, str)) else float(val)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                errors[ptr] = "must be a number"
                continue
            if f.get("min") is not None and num < f["min"]:
                errors[ptr] = f"must be at least {f['min']}"
            if f.get("max") is not None and num > f["max"]:
                errors[ptr] = f"must be at most {f['max']}"
            result[key] = num
        elif kind == "bool":
            if not isinstance(val, bool):
                errors[ptr] = "must be true or false"
        elif kind in ("list", "multiSelect", "orderedList"):
            if not isinstance(val, list):
                errors[ptr] = "must be a list"
        elif kind == "url":
            if not isinstance(val, str) or not (
                val.startswith("http://") or val.startswith("https://")
            ):
                errors[ptr] = "must be an http or https URL"

    return result, errors

class _KVClient:
    def __init__(self, call_json: Callable[..., Any]) -> None:
        self._call = call_json

    def get(self, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
        encoded = urllib.parse.quote(key, safe="")
        res = self._call("GET", f"/ether/plugin-host/kv/{encoded}", allow_404=True)
        return res.get("value") if isinstance(res, dict) else None

    def put(self, key: str, value: str) -> None:
        encoded = urllib.parse.quote(key, safe="")
        self._call("PUT", f"/ether/plugin-host/kv/{encoded}", {"value": str(value)})

    def delete(self, key: str) -> None:
        encoded = urllib.parse.quote(key, safe="")
        self._call("DELETE", f"/ether/plugin-host/kv/{encoded}")

    def list(self, prefix: str = "") -> List[str]:
        q = f"?prefix={urllib.parse.quote(prefix, safe='')}" if prefix else ""
        res = self._call("GET", f"/ether/plugin-host/kv{q}")
        return list(res.get("keys", [])) if isinstance(res, dict) else []

    def usage(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        res = self._call("GET", "/ether/plugin-host/kv-usage")
        return dict(res) if isinstance(res, dict) else {}


MAX_POSTER_BADGE_SETS = 4
MAX_BADGE_ENTRIES_PER_CALL = 500
MAX_BADGE_LABELS_PER_TITLE = 3
MAX_BADGE_LABEL_LEN = 16
POSTER_BADGE_QUOTA_TITLES = 200_000

_BADGE_SET_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$")
_BADGE_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z0-9 +&'./-]+$")
_IMDB_BADGE_RE = re.compile(r"^tt[0-9]{1,12}$")


class PosterBadgeSetMeta(TypedDict, total=False):
    key: str
    label: str
    description: str


class BadgeTitleRef(TypedDict, total=False):
    type: str
    tmdb: int
    imdb: str


class BadgeEntry(TypedDict):
    title: BadgeTitleRef
    labels: List[str]


class BadgeUsage(TypedDict):
    titles: int
    quotaTitles: int


def _check_badge_set_key(set_key: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(set_key, str) or not _BADGE_SET_KEY_RE.match(set_key):
        raise ValueError("badge set key must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$")
    return set_key


def _normalize_badge_label(raw: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        raise ValueError("badge label must be a string")
    upper = "".join(chr(ord(ch) - 32) if "a" <= ch <= "z" else ch for ch in raw)
    if (
        len(upper) < 1
        or len(upper) > MAX_BADGE_LABEL_LEN
        or not upper.strip()
        or not _BADGE_LABEL_RE.match(upper)
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"badge label must be 1..{MAX_BADGE_LABEL_LEN} characters from [A-Z0-9 +&'./-]"
        )
    return upper


def _resolve_badge_title_key(
    title: Dict[str, Any],
    catalog_store: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
) -> str:
    if not isinstance(title, dict):
        raise ValueError("badge title must be an object")
    t_type = title.get("type")
    if t_type not in ("movie", "show"):
        raise ValueError('badge title.type must be "movie" or "show"')
    tmdb_raw = title.get("tmdb")
    tmdb = 0
    if tmdb_raw is not None:
        if isinstance(tmdb_raw, bool) or not isinstance(tmdb_raw, int) or tmdb_raw <= 0:
            raise ValueError("badge title.tmdb must be a positive integer")
        tmdb = tmdb_raw
    imdb_raw = title.get("imdb")
    imdb = ""
    if imdb_raw is not None and imdb_raw != "":
        if not isinstance(imdb_raw, str):
            raise ValueError("badge title.imdb must be a string")
        norm = imdb_raw.strip().lower()
        if not _IMDB_BADGE_RE.match(norm):
            raise ValueError("badge title.imdb must match tt<digits>")
        imdb = norm
    if tmdb == 0 and not imdb:
        raise ValueError("badge title requires tmdb or imdb")
    if tmdb > 0:
        for item in catalog_store.values():
            if item.get("type") == t_type and item.get("tmdbId") == tmdb:
                return str(item.get("id"))
    if imdb:
        for item in catalog_store.values():
            if item.get("type") == t_type and str(item.get("imdbId") or "").lower() == imdb:
                return str(item.get("id"))
    return f"tmdb:{t_type}:{tmdb}" if tmdb > 0 else f"imdb:{t_type}:{imdb}"


def _count_distinct_badge_titles(store: Dict[str, Dict[str, List[str]]]) -> int:
    seen = set()
    for set_map in store.values():
        seen.update(set_map.keys())
    return len(seen)

            "titles": int(res.get("titles", 0)),
            "quotaTitles": int(res.get("quotaTitles", 0)),
        }


MIN_DATA_READ_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_DATA_READ_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_ARCHIVE_READ_ITEMS = 4096

    width: int
    height: int
    format: str

    blob: str
    contentType: str
    width: int
    height: int
    size: int


def _check_rasterize_options(options: Optional[RasterizeOptions]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    if options is None:
        return None
    out: Dict[str, Any] = dict(options)
    for dim in (out.get("width"), out.get("height")):
        if dim is not None and (isinstance(dim, bool) or not isinstance(dim, int) or dim < 0 or dim > 2048):
            raise ValueError("cache.rasterize width and height must be within 0..2048")
    fmt = out.get("format")
    if fmt is not None and fmt not in ("png", "jpeg"):
        raise ValueError("cache.rasterize format must be png or jpeg")
    return out


def _check_data_range(data_range: Dict[str, Any], max_bytes: int = MAX_DATA_READ_BYTES) -> Dict[str, int]:
    offset = data_range.get("offset")
    length = data_range.get("length")
    if (
        isinstance(offset, bool)
        or isinstance(length, bool)
        or not isinstance(offset, int)
        or not isinstance(length, int)
        or offset < 0
        or offset > (1 << 60)
        or length <= 0
        or length > max_bytes
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"Data range needs nonnegative offset and length 1..{max_bytes}")
    return {"offset": offset, "length": length}


def _check_archive_reads(reads: List[ArchiveReadItem], max_bytes: int = MAX_DATA_READ_BYTES) -> List[Dict[str, int]]:
    if not isinstance(reads, list) or len(reads) == 0 or len(reads) > MAX_ARCHIVE_READ_ITEMS:
        raise ValueError(f"archive.read takes 1..{MAX_ARCHIVE_READ_ITEMS} reads")
    normalized: List[Dict[str, int]] = []
    total = 0
    for item in reads:
        member = item.get("member")
        if isinstance(member, bool) or not isinstance(member, int) or member < 0:
            raise ValueError("archive.read member index must be a nonnegative integer")
        rng = _check_data_range(item, max_bytes=max_bytes)
        total += rng["length"]
        if total > max_bytes:
            raise ValueError(f"archive.read requested bytes exceed per-call readBytes limit ({max_bytes})")
        normalized.append({"member": member, "offset": rng["offset"], "length": rng["length"]})
    return normalized


class _RuntimeClient:
    def __init__(self, call_json: Callable[..., Any]) -> None:
        self._call = call_json

    def limits(self) -> RuntimeLimits:
        res = self._call("GET", "/ether/plugin-host/limits")
        return dict(res) if isinstance(res, dict) else {}  # type: ignore[return-value]


class _ArchiveClient:
    def __init__(self, call_json: Callable[..., Any]) -> None:
        self._call = call_json

    def list(self, blob_ref: str) -> List[ArchiveMember]:
        res = self._call("POST", "/ether/plugin-host/data/archive.list", [str(blob_ref)])
        return list(res) if isinstance(res, list) else []

    def open(self, blob_ref: str, member: int, data_range: DataRange) -> bytes:  # noqa: A002
        norm = _check_data_range(data_range)
        res = self._call("POST", "/ether/plugin-host/data/archive.open", [str(blob_ref), int(member), norm])
        return base64.b64decode((res or {}).get("bodyBase64") or "")

    def read(self, blob_ref: str, reads: List[ArchiveReadItem]) -> List[ArchiveReadResult]:
        norm = _check_archive_reads(reads)
        res = self._call("POST", "/ether/plugin-host/data/archive.read", [str(blob_ref), norm])
        rows = res if isinstance(res, list) else []
        return [
            {
                "index": int(row["index"]),
                "member": int(row["member"]),
                "size": int(row["size"]),
                "body": base64.b64decode(row.get("bodyBase64") or ""),
            }
            for row in rows
        ]

    def extract(
        self,
        blob_ref: str,
        member: int,
        options: Optional[ArchiveExtractOptions] = None,
    ) -> ArchiveExtractResult:
        args: List[Any] = [str(blob_ref), int(member)]
        if options is not None:
            args.append(dict(options))
        res = self._call("POST", "/ether/plugin-host/data/archive.extract", args)
        return res if isinstance(res, dict) else {}  # type: ignore[return-value]


class _HttpClient:
    def __init__(self, call_json: Callable[..., Any]) -> None:
        self._call = call_json

    def hash(self, req: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return self._call("POST", "/ether/plugin-host/data/http.hash", [req])

    def fetch_to_cache(self, req: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return self._call("POST", "/ether/plugin-host/data/http.fetchToCache", [req])

    fetchToCache = fetch_to_cache

    def fetch(self, req: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        method = str(req.get("method") or "GET").upper()
        url = str(req["url"])
        headers = dict(req.get("headers") or {})
        body_str = req.get("body")
        data = body_str.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body_str, str) else None
        request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=min(15, max(0.001, float(req.get("timeoutMs", 15000)) / 1000))) as resp:
                raw = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
                out_headers = {k.lower(): v for k, v in resp.headers.items()}
                return {"status": resp.status, "headers": out_headers, "body": raw}
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            raw = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            out_headers = {k.lower(): v for k, v in exc.headers.items()} if exc.headers else {}
            return {"status": exc.code, "headers": out_headers, "body": raw}
